_note: Canonical backlog for Project Io — the authoritative METADATA index of every backlog item.
One item = one object in `items`.
STATUS (authoritative; JSON wins over any prose/glyph disagreement):
designed    (glyph ✓) — design settled, promote-ready.
design-owed (glyph ~) — design still owed; must be settled before promotion.
PRIORITY (ascending): F C B A S SSS.
F=deferred/parked, C=low, B=medium, A=important, S=high, SSS=do-immediately.
`parked:true` is the explicit flag for F-priority items.
DIFFICULTY (1-5): 1=~5min, 2=~20min, 3=~1h, 4=~3h, 5=~12h+ (break a 5 down).
SEQUENCING: `requires` lists BL-XXX ids of backlog items that must land first (supercedes the
old `waits_on` short_name list — v2 schema 2026-06-17). `blocked_on` names a truly-external
prerequisite with no backlog item (third-party dep, real-world gate). An item can be `designed`
and still have unmet `requires`. Both fields are nullable; [] means no dependencies.
WORKFLOW: a `designed` item is PROMOTED into REFINED.md and DELIVERED (see DELIVERY.md).
A `design-owed` item is DESIGNED first (prose settled in `design` field, status flipped).
When work lands, the item is RETAINED here under the terminal status `complete` with a
resolution/completion_note, and design propagates into the authority doc. (Convention updated
2026-07-04: terminal items were once removed; the tooling — gyre.py, progress counts — now
depends on them staying. Do not delete landed entries.)
(Terminal status normalised 2026-08-01: `complete` is the only one. `shipped` was a
synonym with no defined difference — written only by tools/session/ship_items.js and
apply_session_close.js, which now write `complete`; the six items carrying it were
converted. Readers still tolerate the old value, so nothing breaks on an old branch.)
DESIGN PROSE — the `design` field (policy updated 2026-06-17):
- ALL items: prose lives in the `design` field here, not in BACKLOG.md.
- NEW items: author prose here directly. No BACKLOG.md body.
- LEGACY items (pre-2026-06-17): `design: "@BACKLOG.md"` means prose is still in markdown.
Migrate to this field on first edit (design settle or promotion) — do not wait for promotion.
On migration: write prose here, replace the BACKLOG.md body with a tombstone line.
- ON PROMOTION into REFINED.md: delete any remaining BACKLOG.md body (if not yet migrated).
- BACKLOG.md therefore only drains, never grows, and is deleted once empty.
- For designs with rich tables use markdown in the `design` string (tables render fine).
- `design: "@<doc>"` is also valid as a pointer to an authority doc when prose lives there.
VERSION GOAL (policy added 2026-07-08): every NEW item names which version it is FOR via the
`version_goal` field — the minor it targets ("v0.0.9"), the next one ("v0.1.0"), or
"post-v0.1.0" for anything beyond the prototype's remaining arc (see ROADMAP.md for the
live version sequence and themes). This is a goal, not a promise — it may slip a version at
re-sequencing, same as priority. Legacy items predating this policy are not backfilled; treat
a missing `version_goal` as "unset (legacy)", not as "post-v0.1.0".
ARCHIVE — the hot/cold split (policy added 2026-08-02):
This file is the METADATA INDEX and is read ACROSS items far more often than INTO one.
So when an item lands, its narrative fields — design, resolution, completion_note,
progress_note — MOVE OUT to docs/development/archive/backlog-design-<quarter>.json.
The item keeps `design: "@<that path>"` (the pointer form blessed above) plus an
`archived` field naming the cold file. This is the authority time-slice made physical:
backlog.json owns the item while it is open; the cold store and the subject authority
doc own it once it has landed.
- Run it: tools/session/archive_designs.js (Delivery close step, after ship_items.js).
- Read it back: tools/session/backlog_query.js --full, or backlog_view.js — both resolve
the pointer transparently, so an archived item reads exactly like a hot one.
- Reverse it: archive_designs.js --restore [BL-XXX ...]. Nothing is ever deleted.
- AMEND A LANDED ITEM'S PROSE IN THE COLD FILE, not here — the hot file has no copy.
- backlog_lint.js FAILS on an `archived` pointer with no record behind it, and WARNS
when frozen history climbs back over 30% of this file.

items.title: Clarify the time control view
items.summary: Production clock: year+quarter+month/day, a worded days-until-next-quarter countdown (Q2 in 47d), speed curve; Space=pause, 1-5=speed via canvas_command. v0.0.8 polish. [COMPLETE 2026-06-30: econ-tick days-until-next-quarter countdown shipped in the time panel (src/core/app.cpp).]

items.title: Placement-suitability surface (a lens on tile selection, not a strip lens)
items.summary: For a selected/armed building type, tint tiles by validity/affinity (valid highlighted, invalid greyed, thrives-here stronger). NOT an overlay_mode. Design owed: trigger, colour treatment, state model.

items.title: Reach / Logistics-range lens
items.summary: Body-level reach lens: which bodies a corp's trade routes currently connect to, tiered by recency. Standalone lens, distinct from BL-014's flow read. Unblocked — BL-039/BL-088 landed.

items.title: Supply-routes lens — market-connection graph
items.summary: Graph of trade routes between bodies, edge thickness from convoy_count (volume proxy), recency-tiered colour. Aggregated from BL-088's trade_route list, not per-frame. Unblocked — BL-039/BL-088 landed.

items.title: Market lens → market-boundary UI; relocate the price readout
items.summary: Replace market-price map UI with a market-boundary (catchment tint) lens; keep the price-UI code but move it to a menu/selection-accessed lens. Design owed: boundary rendering, price-lens entry point.

items.title: Lens colour-scheme pass (deferred to a colour session)
items.summary: Colourblind-safe palette pass across all lenses (Okabe-Ito categorical / Viridis-style ordered ramp for quantitative), plus on-canvas labels and a Corporation-lens legend. Scoped down from the original two-pass proposal — no added pattern/glyph redundancy channel (Ben's call).

items.title: Tooltip simplification — lens-specific, why not what
items.summary: Reframe tooltips: less data, lens-specific, explain WHY a system behaves (ledgers are for data). The 2026-06-24 accessibility review adds a cognitive-accessibility rationale — a 'why not what' tooltip reduces the interpretive load of the colour-coded lenses, pairing with BL-016's labels/legend. Defer nested tooltips. A large multi-round sweep over every visible entity. Design owed: the per-entity/per-lens content sweep. [COMPLETE 2026-06-30: shipped as lens-contextual hover-card content (src/ui/hover_content.cpp; 3 exemplars Tile×Resource, Building×Supply, Market×Market + graceful fallback). Per-combo coverage is incremental follow-on.]

items.title: Surface multiple markets in the economy / market ledgers
items.summary: Market read surfaces show each market on a body distinctly (per-market breakdown/selector, '1 of N'), so the tile-centred-markets mechanism is visible. User flagged vital. Design owed: per-market table/selector layout.

items.title: Canvas hit-testing for buildings / units / markets
items.summary: Add canvas hit-testing for building/unit/market kinds (today only body/tile). Depends on those entities being drawn as selectable markers first (promoted then cancelled 2026-06-14).

items.title: Lens-driven selection resolution
items.summary: Resolve the entity under the pointer through the active lens (specificity stack building->listing->tile->body, lowest valid wins per a lens resolution table) and route to the lens's ledger. Tile/body rows buildable now; marker rows blocked on hit-testing.

items.title: Economy warm-start pre-generation pass — surface auto-buy / auto-sell
items.summary: Pre-generation settle so the economy opens at/near steady state, with a legible readout of what is auto-sold (excess) and auto-bought at start. Builds on the v0.0.4 warm-start. Design owed: settle-ticks, the readout.

items.title: Seed multiple market centres from capitals / population
items.summary: Mechanism landed 2026-06-16; remaining is generation seeding >1 market centre per body (today one degenerate market). Design owed (deferred to population layer): centre count/seeds + Market lens per-catchment tint.

items.title: Preferential purchasing (choosing counterparties)
items.summary: Replace pooled clearing with a per-(body,resource) matched ORDER BOOK (price-time priority, EMA anchor price preserved) + a buyer counterparty preference (ranked/avoid as a matching bias). Contracts/tariffs deferred to v0.2.0. Blocked on Layer 5 reachability.

items.title: Inter-body / international markets
items.summary: Each body keeps its own market/price; bodies couple ONLY through Supply convoys (market-to-market, mode-gated, Euclidean space distance). First build is a minimal feasibility probe of the coupling alone (no space gameplay). Blocked on Layer 5.

items.title: Supply routing — convoys (Layer 5)
items.summary: Convoy entity (source/dest market, mode, cargo, progress, per-unit-distance logistical cost); auto-dispatch default, player-directed exception (space launches MUST be player-directed). Umbrella; decomposes 1->2->3->4 serial + 5 (lens) disjoint. The largest remaining v0.1.0 build (a 5); v0.0.7's whole theme.

items.title: Resource generation — full-set deposit authoring + scarcity (v0.2)
items.summary: Extend deposit authoring from the 7-resource subset to the full raw set via a seeded per-resource rarity scalar [0,1] (raw-tier only) modulating frequency/magnitude over terrain affinity. Corrected 2026-07-21 (Sprint 1 procgen review): already shipped — this entry was stale, left at design-owed after landing.

items.title: Habitability gates max workforce, not production directly
items.summary: Habitability caps a building's max workforce fraction (not output directly): >~0.6 -> 100% base; below, reduced. Tech later raises above 100% (0.99 -> ~250%). Design owed: the curve, the over-100% tech model.

items.title: Building rules — stricter placement & a per-building justification process
items.summary: Placement too loose (buildings infinite, Port anywhere). Define stricter per-building rules (counts/terrain/adjacency/finite slots) + a user-approved per-building justification table; building-ledger-as-secondary-window direction. USER RESPONSE REQUIRED. Design owed.

items.title: Construction pricing — buildings cost resources (per-building, approved)
items.summary: Buildings cost resources to construct, set per-building and user-approved (a documented cost table). Couples to the labour/material split and the construction spend. Design owed: the per-building cost table + approval pass.

items.title: Logistics network & infrastructure model
items.summary: Infrastructure gates+costs each convoy mode (land<sea<air<space): land ungated (road=optional tile-attribute cost-reducer), sea gated on Port, air on Airfield (deferred building), space on Launchpad+Orbital Port. Capacity deferred. Emanation 'fuel' model noted as the growth direction (Shadow Empire feel).

items.title: Layer 4 — population centres + building management (index)
items.summary: Umbrella index (NOT promotable) over the population + building-management layer. Fully decomposed 2026-06-15 into its child items (POPULATION_STATIC_MVP, POPULATION_DYNAMIC, WORKFORCE_POOL_STEP2, the ledger family, BUILDING_MANAGEMENT). No design owed at this level. [COMPLETE 2026-06-30: umbrella index; all child items (population static/dynamic, workforce pool, ledger family, building management) shipped across v0.0.5–v0.0.7.]

items.title: Generate the saturated nation-owned background substrate
items.summary: Per-tile substrate_density [0,1] on tile_component; nation_substrate aggregate (background supply+demand arrays) in world; population-ripple generation pass; economy tick injects substrate supply/demand into per-body markets. Static for v0.0.6. Continuous density model. Lens visual deferred to v0.2.
items.design:
@docs/development/archive/backlog-design-2026-Q2.json

## 2026-08-10 - SUPERSEDED IN APPROACH by BL-365 (not reopened)

Ben, 2026-08-10: *"My call is to replace the substrate entirely."* What this item built - a
nation-owned background substrate injected into the clearing tick - is being replaced by **real
background industry** (BL-365, v0.1.13): actual firms with actual buildings, so market saturation is
emergent rather than asserted once per tick.

This item stays `complete` and is not reopened. It did its job, and the *requirement* it served -
that the player is a small participant in a saturated market rather than the whole economy - is
carried forward unchanged. Only the mechanism changes. See BL-365 for the replacement and for why
the ownership question resolves to corporations rather than nations.

items.title: Tile generation refinements (deferred — deep models owed)
items.summary: Generation-mechanics passes only (deposit data half moved to RESOURCE_GENERATION_FULL_SET, now complete): smooth band transitions + coastline refinement (buildable, cosmetic) and speculative orbital-derivation + tectonic landforms (still design-owed, beyond v0.1.0). Settled 2026-07-21 (Sprint 1 procgen review): the six-pass pipeline stays fixed; every extension here lands as a sibling pass, same convention BL-170 (rivers) established this sprint.

items.title: Rename Faction → Country
items.summary: Full disentanglement of Faction from Country: Country for all nation/territory usages; `faction_colour()` → `corp_colour()`. Explicitly NOT a blanket replace — corporation usages keep the corp naming.

items.title: Country generation — more countries, generated 'in history'
items.summary: More countries than today's Voronoi partition, with a sense of history: over-seed + light merge (Pass 1b growth weights, Pass 2c 'in history' merges) gives a strongly varied, irregular-bordered political layer. Landed fc7c62b (18 seeds -> 14 nations); retuned 2026-07-08 to 34 seeds -> 24 nations for a richer map. No history/event-log mechanic — the variance itself reads as implied age.

items.title: Deferred — nation behaviour & production passes
items.summary: The nation SYSTEM (tax, licences, war, infrastructure), sentiment graph, historical fragmentation (exclaves/disputed zones), non-Kepler jurisdiction. Out of prototype scope; design owed when in scope. SETTLED 2026-08-02 by redistribution: three of the four parts moved out today. Tax and the licence gate are LAWS (BL-155 margin-modifier and gate families); the sentiment graph is BL-158 (asymmetric per-pair); historical fragmentation folded into BL-218, where a real settlement sim yields exclaves for free instead of decorating a Voronoi output. What remains is the RUNTIME NATION ACTOR — applying laws, issuing licences, the infrastructure scalar and the war flag — which is nation AI and stays prohibited until BL-094. The line is now one sentence: BL-155/BL-158 give nations things to HAVE, this item gives them things to DO. Difficulty 5->3, no longer needs breaking down. Stays parked.

items.title: Nav slot open/close colour not in sync when panel closed via X button
items.summary: Nav rail slots show an active (highlighted) state driven by show_* booleans in ui_state. When a ledger panel is closed via its X button, ImGui sets the bool false one frame later so the slot de-highlights correctly. However, if a second panel opens while a first is already open, neither closes the other — both slots show active simultaneously. Fix: when a nav slot is toggled ON, clear all other show_* panel booleans so at most one panel is active at a time (exclusive-open model), OR document that simultaneous panels are intended and the highlight is per-panel not per-slot.

items.title: Economy bankruptcy test — calibrate costs to a 10–20 year runway
items.summary: Headless harness that runs economy ticks from world-gen to bankruptcy (cash <= 0), records tick count per run, and outputs a per-building / per-resource data table. Goal: tune costs so the average player goes bankrupt in 10–20 in-game years without intervention — use the data to derive sensible build costs and running expenses.

items.title: Cross-platform build (Linux + Windows)
items.summary: Linux+Windows build. Source already Linux-clean (FetchContent deps, LUA_USE_POSIX guarded) except src/ui/fonts.cpp's hardcoded Windows font paths; fix = bundle assets/fonts + SDL_GetBasePath prepend, Windows paths as fallback. Headless tier builds anywhere; GitHub Actions both-OS headless CI as the guard. Dev moves to Linux (dual-boot); visual-verify offscreen (dummy+software renderer / Xvfb) is a deferred spike. [COMPLETE 2026-06-30: native Linux GCC-14 build confirmed (C language enabled, sol2 v3.5.0); Windows + dual-GCC CI green; advisory Xvfb visual-verify job added.]

items.title: Git hygiene for the Cowork-shell bridge (line endings + native-commit rule)
items.summary: Two git footguns when running git inside the Cowork shell (VM bridge): CRLF blobs vs LF mount -> whole-file diff churn; .git blocks unlink/rename -> stale lock files + unsafe ref writes. Fix: add .gitattributes (* text=auto) + one-time renormalize for the CRLF half; standing rule that git WRITES run from native Claude Code / terminal, never the Cowork shell. Part 2 dissolves under native Linux dev (BL-057).

items.title: Selectable entity markers — buildings, units, market centres
items.summary: On-canvas marker entities (buildings, units, market centres) drawn as distinct, clickable/selectable ImDrawList glyphs at world positions. Prerequisite for canvas hit-testing to extend beyond tile/body kind. Design owed: marker shapes, z-order, hover-zone size, registration contract.

items.title: Hover-card UI primitive — transient floating detail card
items.summary: A transient floating card that appears on tile/entity hover — distinct from the pinned Selection panel. Lighter than a tooltip (richer content, brief delay) but dismisses on mouse-off. Prerequisite for the tooltip-simplification sweep (BL-020). Design owed: content contract, animation, relationship to Selection panel.

items.title: Application-driven mouse — scriptable cursor override for deterministic capture
items.summary: A verify/app-controlled synthetic cursor so the real OS mouse position cannot leak into --verify captures (hover highlight + hover-card perturb the frame -> flaky goldens). Also the foundation for scripted pointer input (move/click/drag) in the verify harness. Design owed: synthetic-vs-real source switch, global hover-suppress vs explicit positioning, click/drag API surface. [COMPLETE 2026-06-30: application-driven mouse (ui_state::mouse + verify Lua mouse()/hover_tile()) shipped; OS cursor suppressed in --verify captures.]

items.title: Full hotkey system — unified, rebindable keymap + discoverability
items.summary: Replace the ad-hoc, partly-hardcoded input (canvas_command vocabulary + Space=pause, 1-5 speed, lens cycle) with a unified hotkey system: a central action->binding keymap, rebindable, discoverable (help/cheat-sheet overlay), covering canvas nav, lens selection, time control, ledger toggles, and build. Design owed: binding storage, conflict/chord handling, the help surface, context scoping, how it subsumes canvas_command. Reframed 2026-06-24 as the motor-accessibility half of the accessibility strand — keyboard-complete, rebindable operation is the top motor-access win. [COMPLETE 2026-06-30: unified hotkey dispatch (s_bindings, dispatch_action) + F1 cheat-sheet overlay shipped (src/core/app.cpp, canvas_command.*).]

items.title: Accessibility & legibility baseline — UI scale + secondary-text contrast
items.summary: Legibility baseline from the 2026-06-24 accessibility UX review: a global UI-scale control (ImGui FontGlobalScale / font re-load) and a secondary-text contrast pass to clear WCAG AA on dim header/label/ledger text. The non-colour half of accessibility — colour-vision stays in BL-016, motor/keyboard in BL-062. Design owed: scale storage/persistence, the FontGlobalScale-vs-refont tradeoff, a measured contrast token audit, whether a docs/ui/ACCESSIBILITY.md is warranted. [NOTE 2026-06-30: this is the WCAG-contrast + UI-scale item; distinct from the shipped tester-legibility trend plots now tracked as BL-066. The 'BL-063' label on the trend-plots commits predates this slot's reassignment.]

items.title: Clock speed buttons — Roman numeral labels
items.summary: Relabel the five speed buttons from Arabic numerals (1–5) to Roman numerals (I–V). Roman numerals are the established convention for speed tiers in grand strategy games and read more naturally as an ordinal scale than multiplicative fractions. [COMPLETE 2026-06-30: speed buttons relabelled I–V, pause as || (src/core/app.cpp).]

items.title: Selection info element — full-width bottom bar layout
items.summary: Redesign the Selection info element from a narrow bottom-left pinned panel to a full-width bar spanning the bottom of the screen, tall enough to show an entity portrait alongside multiple content sections simultaneously in one view. [COMPLETE 2026-06-30: full-width bottom selection bar with portrait column + summary/lens-supplement sections shipped (src/ui/selection_panel.cpp).]

items.title: Tester-legibility trend plots — balance/market history graphs
items.summary: Income/expenditure and market-price history captured into capped ring buffers and drawn as sparkline trend plots in the Economy panel and Market Ledger (Okabe-Ito palette). [COMPLETE 2026-06-30: shipped in the v0.0.7 batch; originally committed under the 'BL-063' label before that slot was reassigned to the accessibility item — recorded here to keep the shipped history queryable.]

items.title: Survey system — bodies start unsurveyed; survey action reveals tile map + deposit bands
items.summary: v0.0.8 discovery strand. Bodies start unsurveyed: only type, orbital position and grid size are known. The player dispatches a survey (credits upfront) that plays out over sim ticks, revealing the body REGION-BY-REGION until surface + deposit bands are known; exact deposit amounts still wait for first extraction-site placement. Cost and duration scale with body size AND distance from home. No concurrency cap — credit cost is the throttle. Earth/home start surveyed. DESIGN SETTLED 2026-06-30 (BL-067).

items.title: Visibility model — competitor info asymmetry (markers public, production/stockpile private, markets public)
items.summary: v0.0.8 discovery strand. Competitor information asymmetry as a READ-TIME access policy over existing data (no new stored state). Rival building markers visible only where the body's survey has revealed their region; rival hover cards show type + owner only; selecting a rival building opens a dedicated competitor panel with explicit 'private' placeholders for production/stockpile; market aggregates + prices stay public (the intelligence channel). Uniform rule: anything not player-owned is opaque. Requires BL-067. DESIGN SETTLED 2026-06-30 (BL-068).
items.notes: Unblocked 2026-06-30: BL-067 (survey region mask) delivered — the rival-marker region-reveal predicate can now layer on the survey gate.

items.title: Population legibility — surface habitability→workforce reasoning in lens / hover / selection
items.summary: v0.0.8 discovery strand — surfacing only, no new mechanics. Makes the existing habitability→workforce feedback legible so the player can reason about siting. Surfaced in the Selection panel, hover cards, AND the Population lens. Workforce cap shown as an absolute number. The Population lens is RE-KEYED from raw habitability to workforce efficiency via a shared workforce_efficiency(habitability) helper that the economy system also uses (so the lens shows exactly the consequence the sim applies). DESIGN SETTLED 2026-06-30 (BL-069).

items.title: In-app system menu — Exit Game / pause without keyboard
items.summary: There is no in-app menu for application-level control: today the only way to leave the game is the OS window close button (Windows-only chrome; the window is a plain SDL_WINDOW_RESIZABLE in app.cpp) or a keyboard shortcut. The player wants a minimal, clickable system container — at minimum an Exit Game affordance, reachable without memorising hotkeys and consistent across platforms. Distinct from BL-062 (the keyboard hotkey system) and from the nav-rail ledger menus (MENU.md): those are the keyboard layer and the per-system ledgers; this is the application/session shell (start, pause, exit). Design owed: the surface (top menu bar vs. corner gear button vs. centred pause/system modal), what it contains in the prototype (Exit Game at minimum; likely Resume/Pause; possibly New/Restart), whether a confirm-on-exit is wanted, and how it relates to a future title/main screen.

items.title: Build legibility — selected-tile affordances + 'why not here' placement reasons
items.summary: Gameplay-clarity strand (filed 2026-06-30): 'it's not clear where buildings can be built'. BL-010's placement-suitability surface tints tiles only once a build is ARMED; the player still can't tell what a tile affords beforehand, nor WHY a tinted-invalid tile is rejected. Surfacing only, no new placement mechanics: (1) a selected-tile affordance readout (terrain, deposits subject to survey state, territory owner, and which building types thrive / are valid / are invalid here); (2) rejection reasons — placement_rules returns a REASON (wrong terrain / no deposit / occupied / outside territory / slot full) instead of a bare bool, surfaced when an armed build hovers an invalid tile.

items.title: Full budget breakdown — income vs expenditure itemised + projected runway
items.summary: v0.0.9 core strand (budget clarity) — directly answers 'how does the player make a profit'. The budget loop already computes balance += income − expenditure − maintenance − wages per corp (budget_system.hpp) but retains NO category split. Capture the four flows (and ideally by building type / resource / logistics) into the economy report, then surface an itemised income-vs-expenditure breakdown plus a running balance shown against a PROJECTED time-to-zero so the player feels the pressure and can act before bankruptcy.

items.title: Debt-interest system — interest accrues on negative balance, visible as a budget line
items.summary: v0.0.9 strand. When a corp balance goes negative, interest accrues each tick — the econ_bankruptcy harness (BL-056) already models this for calibration, but no player-facing surface exists (grep for 'interest' in src/ returns nothing). Add the interest charge to apply_budget and surface it as a DISTINCT expenditure line in the budget breakdown so the player sees when they have entered a self-accelerating decline.

items.title: Per-building profitability readout — make each building's unit economics legible
items.summary: Gameplay-clarity strand (filed 2026-06-30) — the most direct answer to 'how does the player make a profit'. Today the player sees only the corp-wide balance; they cannot tell WHICH buildings earn and which bleed. Attribute the four budget flows ([[BL-072]]) to the individual building and show its net per-tick contribution (output sales − input cost − wages − maintenance) in the Selection panel for a selected building, so siting and recipe decisions become legible at the unit level.

items.title: Corp × terrain viability test matrix — every generated corp has a buildable, profitable chain
items.summary: Testing strand (filed 2026-06-30): 'unit tests for different corps in different generated terrains'. A new headless harness (verifier-headless pattern) that sweeps multiple world seeds and, for each generated corporation on its assigned body, asserts a viable economic start: starting assets sit on legal terrain, the corp's industrial focus has at least one VALID placement on its body, and at least one output resource has a market — i.e. a generated corp can actually build something profitable on the terrain it was dealt. Guards against world-gen handing a corp a body where it is economically stranded.

items.title: Display options window — resolution / fullscreen / vsync, persisted
items.summary: Pre-playtest QOL: the player had no way to set or remember the window size/mode. The OS window is already SDL_WINDOW_RESIZABLE (free drag-resize worked), but the startup size was hard-coded 1280x720 with no fullscreen/vsync control and nothing persisted. Adds an F10 Options window (resolution presets, fullscreen, vsync) that applies live and persists to options.cfg, plus capture of free drag-resizes. Distinct from BL-070 (in-app system menu: exit/pause) which is the session shell; this is the display-settings surface.

items.title: Era 1 tech / quest system — structure, itemisation schema & gate model (design)
items.summary: Design strand (Ben, 2026-07-01; six open questions resolved 2026-07-08) — the quest-based tech system named in concept.md. The 2026-07-08 session RE-FRAMED the Era model: ERAS ARE CATASTROPHIC EVENTS (war, satellite cascade) arriving on the world clock — the external clock; tech can move faster but never opens an Era. Capstones open QUEST TREES, not Eras (the ERAS.md Rocketry+Launchpad+propellant set is re-read as gating a quest tree). The THREADING INSIGHT survives: gate = quest = tech, one condition-set object, so a tech can gate on an ECONOMIC state (reserved for capstones + a few marquee nodes). Structure settled: quests are mostly binary trees with dead-end leaves; standing lines never gate Eras but CAN gate quest lines; research capacity comes from dedicated buildings or scales with industry (mix = playtest); payoffs mostly tangible (building/recipe/technique), passive buffs sparing; cross-quest prereqs allowed sparingly + marked. SCOPE: all post-prototype (even the lean gate-tech) — prototype keeps the hard-coded Era arrangement; ROADMAP already excludes Research. A follow-up brief session (2026-07-08, v0.2.0-horizon) resolved A–C: Era-event timing is a SEEDED DATE with a VISIBLE COUNTDOWN; the boundary event SHOCKS MARKETS + DESTROYS SOME INFRASTRUCTURE + UNLOCKS THE NEW ERA'S QUEST TREES (all three together); 'gate quest' renames to KEYSTONE QUEST (apply on the next itemisation pass). Resolutions + sketch + worked Propellant Loop table live in docs/research/ERA1_TECH_LANDSCAPE.md. A mock tree (53 techs) is already visible in a build via the F9 viewer. No open questions remain at design-sketch depth; itemisation is the next step, deferred to v0.2.0. SETTLED 2026-08-02: the status was STALE — it claimed an owed set remained (Era-event mechanics) while the section immediately below resolves A/B/C in the same 2026-07-08 session, and the "Next: resolve A-C" line refers to items already resolved above it. Same class as BL-040 in Sprint 1: stale bookkeeping, not open design. BL-156 (settled today) supplies the shared condition_set this item gate model inherits wholesale, and tabulates the boundary — BL-156 owns the OBJECT, this owns the SYSTEM. I want a heavy hand in what actual nodes there are, however you are certainly capable of drafting the initial tree'). Draft lives in docs/research/ERA1_TECH_LANDSCAPE.md - The Era 1 tree - first draft: five sectors (Launch / Volatiles / Mobility / Yards / Extraction) x three rings (Reach / Foothold / Industry), Power-Automation kept as a standing line not a sector, ~45 objects, four keystone forks each OPENED BY A DEED (Ten Flights / The First Tank / The First Truss / The Empty Shift). **Status:** design-owed — shape settled 2026-07-01; the six sketch questions **resolved 2026-07-08** (mobile design session, Ben); a smaller owed set remains (Era-event mechanics, below). The rich design store is **`docs/research/ERA1_TECH_LANDSCAPE.md`** — § 'Tech-tree structure — first sketch (2026-07-01)' for the structure, § 'Resolutions — design session (2026-07-08)' for the decisions (newest-dated wins where they differ); this field is the index summary.

### The Era reframe (2026-07-08, supersedes the sketch's gate model)
- **Eras are catastrophic events on the world clock** — e.g. a war, a satellite/Kessler cascade. The world moves on whether or not the player is ready (the Terra Invicta external-clock lesson, now literal). Tech can move *faster* than the Era clock but never opens an Era.
- **Capstones open quest trees, not Eras.** The `ERAS.md` Rocketry + Launchpad + propellant condition set is re-read as gating a new *quest tree* ('these should have been recorded as gating new quest trees' — Ben). The threading insight survives: gate = quest = tech, one condition-set object over the vocabulary (`research` / `structure` / `stockpile` / `market` / `surplus` / `era` / line-depth).
- **Determinism:** Era events must be seeded/deterministic — no random ruptures.
- `ERAS.md` is deliberately *not* edited yet (authority time-slices); the reframe lives here until work lands.

### Resolutions (2026-07-08)
1. **Quest shape:** mostly a **binary tree** (branching ≤ 2, no re-converging mesh) with **dead-end leaves** (tier chains, optional techs) carrying depth.
2. **Standing lines:** never gate Eras (nothing does, under the reframe); **can gate quest lines** — a quest tree's availability may require standing-line depth.
3. **Build coupling is on research *generation*:** capacity from dedicated buildings (R&D Lab) or scaling with industry — mix is a playtest-tuning item. **Payoffs mostly tangible** (new building / production method / gathering technique), passive buffs sparing — rebalances the sketch's ~13/25 `efficiency` audit toward new-method payoffs.
4. **Cross-quest prereqs:** allowed, sparingly, visually marked (Depot→Orbital Port, Rig→Automation as tabled).
5. **Economic gates:** every capstone + 1–2 marquee nodes per Era; not liberal (stall risk — the capital/runway lesson).
6. **Scope: all post-prototype** — even the lean gate-tech waits past v0.1.0; the prototype keeps the hard-coded Era arrangement. ROADMAP already excludes Research; ERAS ↔ ROADMAP reconcile only when post-prototype work lands.

### Era-event mechanics — resolved (2026-07-08, brief follow-up, v0.2.0-horizon)
A. **Timing:** a seeded date per campaign (deterministic), with a visible in-UI countdown once conditions near it — the Terra Invicta external-clock lesson made literal.
B. **Boundary effects (all three fire together):** shocks nation demand/market prices; selectively destroys some buildings/infrastructure (satellite cascade → orbital assets, war → surface facilities); unlocks the new Era's quest trees. Not purely additive — the event is a shock the player manages.
C. **Terminology:** 'gate quest' → **keystone quest**, matching the Propellant Loop's existing language. Applied on the next itemisation pass, not retroactively in the doc's earlier sections.

### Retained from the sketch
Two quest kinds (gate quests vs standing lines: Logistics / Military / Economy-Automation, which persist and deepen); ~25 techs/quest ≈ ~10 inventions + ~15 tiers; the itemisation schema (quest + tech records, every field a tech-tree UI element); the `payoff` taxonomy (gate > resource > building > recipe > efficiency > enabling); cost model B (S/M/L/XL, default M); the worked **Propellant Loop** quest whose capstone gates on a sustained propellant *surplus*. Provenance corrections (DRACO cancelled → parked propulsion capstone; launch vs ISRU partly rivals; asteroid-mining bust = capital/runway failure → long payback curves) sourced in the doc.

**Next:** resolve A–C (another design session — mobile-friendly), then itemise the quest map post-prototype. No implementation item is minted for v0.1.0 (resolution 6). This item stays the design home.

**Mock landed (2026-07-08, same session):** the sketch is now *visible in a build* — `scripts/tech_tree.lua` (Propellant Loop worked + Era 0/1 stubs + standing lines, 53 techs), `world/tech_tree.{hpp,cpp}` (registry + sol2 loader), and a read-only **F9 viewer** (`ui/tech_tree_panel`). Display only — no research state, no sim coupling; resolution 6 (system post-prototype) stands. Iterate the tree by editing the Lua file alone.

items.title: Product market is inert — capped prices, flat exogenous demand, raw gluts to zero
items.summary: Playtest finding (2026-07-01, 30-year headless econ sweep): the market clears trivially. Product prices climb to a fixed cap by ~yr15 and never move again (Steel 32.00, Refined Fuel 40.00, Food Rations 24.00) while product supply never grows (Steel stuck at 32u, Fuel/Rations at 0). Meanwhile raw extraction floods a flat exogenous demand (~1056/good regardless of world state), pinning ~9 raw prices at 0.00 (Coal, Silica, Copper, Rare Earth, Stone, Timber, Sand, Clay, Peat). Demand responds to nothing, so there is no price discovery and no scarcity tension — the 'too easy to work' gap in the loop the prototype is meant to validate. Design-owed: what demand should be a function of. [DESIGNED 2026-07-07: population as the demand substrate (tiered elastic basket + bounded growth), abstract nation capacity as supply, price band kept.]

## 2026-08-10 - MECHANISM superseded by BL-365; REQUIREMENTS carried forward

The elastic substrate this item built (`inject_substrate_demand`: a price-elastic per-capita basket
against an abstract capacity-capped supply clearing to 90%) is removed by **BL-365** (v0.1.13),

(differentiated, price-elastic demand), R2 (a live margin) and BL-112 R1 (the margin is a fillable
path to profit) all still have to hold - but emergently, from real firms producing and real
population consuming, rather than from an injection with a `clearing_fraction` constant. BL-365's
calibration target (production >= 0.90 x demand) is deliberately this item's own figure, so the gap
is preserved by construction.

One caution this item's gate hands forward, recorded as NR-156: `pregame_balance_harness` currently
passes BL-112 R1 off a price pegged at exactly 4.00x base - the hard ceiling of `resolve_price`'s
band - rather than off a discovered margin. Under real industry a pegged good means nobody produces
it, so BL-365 must treat that as a failure rather than inherit it as a pass.

items.title: Extraction boom-bust vs steady processing — corp fate fixed at generation, no competitive feedback
items.summary: Playtest finding (2026-07-01, 30-year sweep): finite deposit depletion (v0.0.4, by design) makes extraction corps boom then plateau/decline (Corix 65k→162k@yr20→161k@yr30; FararAthar peaks yr20 then falls; Exoar plateaus), while processing corps grind up linearly forever (player 'Genom', steel, +~880/yr steady). A corp on a zero-priced output just bleeds (Faros-Yelen −320/decade). Net: a corp's whole trajectory is essentially fixed at generation by which tile/resource it spawned on — no price feedback, competition, or adaptation erodes a leader or rescues a laggard. The live form of the BL-075 'reachable market / profitable chain' concern. items.title: Player-identity pivot — the player is a NATIONAL PRIVATE MILITIA, private companies as contracted suppliers (supersedes the governing-body framing)
items.summary: REWRITTEN 2026-08-10 (Sprint 8, NR-120). The player is a national private militia — armed, national in allegiance, but not the state. It does not legislate; it PROCURES: raises and fields force, and buys the equipment to do it from private companies that are now arm's-length COUNTERPARTIES rather than the player's own economic arm. This replaces the 2026-08-03 'governing body' framing outright, not an Era-0 reading of it. The three calls this rewrite had to make: (1) the militia is a private force CHARTERED BY one of the ~43 generated nations, not itself one of the 43 — nation generation is untouched, a militia is a new entity type that names a home nation; (2) the shared treasury does NOT survive — the militia holds its own treasury, funded by its home nation's mandate/subsidy plus operating revenue, and spends it contracting companies who can quote, delay, or refuse; (3) the retired v0.1.x design test ('does this reach military as well as economic outcomes?') is replaced by 'does this change what the militia can FIELD, or what it must ANSWER TO?' — procurement and accountability are the militia's two axes, in place of law/policy/science as levers. Difficulty and priority held at 5 / A pending Ben's review of this rewrite.
items.design:
**Status:** designed — settled 2026-07-04 with Ben over a three-call Q&A (identity / coupling / spine). Resolves the long-open player-identity question in CONCEPT.md ('a corporate OR nation-state entity ... a single, committed choice once tradeoffs are weighed'). **Parked for the v0.2.0 arc** (post-v0.1.0): design is settled ahead of sequence (permitted — design may settle early; only implementation and authority-doc propagation wait for the cut).

### The decision
For v0.2.0 the player pivots from a corporation to the **nation** as the strategic actor, owning the three systems that do not sit right on a single corporation — **research, military, and intelligence**. The corporation stays the **economic** actor: the nation charters corporations, and the player-nation is **prototyped as a single chartered corp** (= today's player corp), so the entire v0.0.x economy loop survives intact and the nation is a thin strategic layer *above* it, not a re-plumb. Clean division: **nation = strategic choices (research / force / intel); chartered corp = economic choices (build / trade)** — each still justifying itself by feeding Trade or Conflict.

### Settled calls (Ben, 2026-07-04)
1. **Player identity — one of the generated nations.** The player IS one of the 14 Voronoi nations (NATION_GENERATION.md), not a bolted-on special case. Its broad industrial base stays **AI-run background** exactly as today, so the **economic premise holds unchanged** (GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § The economic premise) and the player never micromanages the saturated economy. Economic agency = the chartered corp; strategic agency = the new nation layer. Because the player is the *same kind of entity* as its rivals, **symmetrical rules** (CONCEPT.md § Symmetrical rules) apply cleanly and **BL-054 nation behaviour** is promoted from background stub to first-class — every AI nation runs the same nation layer.
2. **Charter coupling — tight / shared treasury (prototype-of-1).** With a single chartered corp, the corp's treasury **is** the nation's economic arm: one linked balance funds building / trade AND research / military / intel. The corp↔nation split is therefore one of **agency layer** (which surface you act through), not of money. **1→N evolution note:** the shared treasury is a prototype-of-1 simplification; once a nation charters *multiple* corps it no longer holds, and the existing **tax-as-automated-layer** thread (CORPORATION_GENERATION.md § Open items) returns as the funding coupling — the nation taxes its chartered corps into a distinct national budget. Recorded so the tight choice does not ossify.
3. **v0.2.0 spine — Military.** The nation strategic layer leads with **standing forces / conflict**, not research or intel. Risk + rationale: Conflict is the **least-designed pillar** (today a data-model stub, excluded from the prototype — TECH_FOUNDATIONS), so it carries the most design risk — but it is the most distinctive Era-0 → 'WW3-scale rupture' payoff (CONCEPT.md § Eras) and the cleanest Trade→Conflict link (the nation raises and commands forces from the shared treasury; materiel is drawn from the chartered corp's production and supply lines are live targets — CONCEPT § Combat). Research (BL-087) and intelligence (the DISCOVERY.md substrate) follow in later v0.2.x minors.

### The economic-premise reconciliation (closed)
The risk flagged at capture — does elevating the player to nation-level force them to manage the broad saturated economy? — is closed by call 1: the player-nation's broad economy stays AI-run background, identical to how the 14 nations already carry it. The player still plays as a specialist through one chartered corp; the nation layer sits *above* the economy loop, it does not replace it. Premise and the 14-nation background mass both intact.

### Scope this promotes (the v0.2.0 cost)
- **BL-054 (nation behaviour)** — parked stub → load-bearing: AI nations must run the same nation layer the player does (symmetry).
- **A new conflict / military design item** — none exists today; the Military-first spine needs one authored at v0.2.0 promotion (nation force model, materiel↔production link, supply-line targeting). Conflict graduates from data-model stub to designed pillar.
- **Symmetrical rules** become load-bearing at the nation tier.

### Child items to create at v0.2.0 promotion (NOT now — avoid a parked cascade)
- Nation strategic layer + shared-treasury wiring (chartered-corp-as-economic-arm seam).
- Military / conflict design (the spine) — first subsystem.
- BL-054 promotion to playable nation behaviour.
- Research (BL-087) + intelligence re-homing — later v0.2.x.

### Authority propagation (on landing, NOT now)
CONCEPT.md (identity committed to nation-level, chartered-corp-prototyped-as-1), SYSTEMS.md (nation as the strategic layer over chartered corps; Research / Military / Intel owned at the nation tier), GENERATION_STRATEGY.md + CORPORATION_GENERATION.md (player-nation = one of the 14; chartered-corp origin; shared-treasury → tax at 1→N). Do NOT edit these now — authority time-slicing; v0.1.0 not cut.

### Delivery note
Design settled 2026-07-04 (this session); item flips design-owed → designed but stays **parked (F)** — implementation is v0.2.0, to be promoted on the next cut.

## 2026-08-03 — the reason, stated by Ben, and what it changes

Ben: *"the aim that we're going for now, is to really play as a governing body. The reason for
that is that it allows law, policy and science to use military might - not just economic."*

Everything in the 2026-07-04 settlement above stands. What is new is the **justification**, and
it is load-bearing rather than decorative — it explains why the pivot is the aim rather than an
option, and it retroactively gives the v0.1.x stub band its purpose.

### The argument

A corporation's levers are all economic. It builds, trades, prices, hires. Law, policy and
science *exist* for a corporation only as constraints imposed from outside — things done to it.
So a corporate player can be given a laws system and a tech system, and both remain flavour on
top of an economy: a law changes a number in your cost model; a technology unlocks a building.
Neither reaches force.

A **governing body** inverts that. Law, policy and science become instruments it *wields*, and
crucially they can be pointed at **military might** as well as at the economy:

- **Law** — conscription, requisition, embargo, war powers. A law that raises an army is a
  fundamentally different object from a law that changes a tax rate, and only a governing body
  can pass either.
- **Policy** — force posture, alliance, deterrence, where the standing army stands. Policy with
  no military to point at is just budgeting.
- **Science** — the research that produces weapons and logistics, not only refineries. Research
  owned at the nation tier is the classic grand-strategy engine; research owned by a
  corporation is a tech tree of factories.

**This is the Conflict pillar's route to being load-bearing.** The house rule is that every
system justifies itself by feeding **Trade or Conflict** (io-standing-rules § Tone). Under a
corporate player, laws/techs/politics could only ever feed Trade — which is why Conflict has
stayed the least-designed pillar and kept sliding. Under a governing body they feed both, and
the 2026-07-04 call that **Military anchors the pivot first** stops being a risky preference
and becomes the obvious consequence.

### What it changes about the v0.1.x stub band

ROADMAP's v0.1.2–v0.1.5 (laws BL-155, techs BL-156, military BL-157, politics BL-158) were
themed *"ponder and stub what the expanded prototype will need"* — deliberately vague because
nobody had said what they were for. They now have a single answer: **they are the governing
body's levers.** That gives each stub a design test it did not have:

> Does this system reach **military** as well as economic outcomes? If it can only ever change
> a cost or a price, it is being designed for the corporate player we are pivoting away from.

Apply that test when each minor is reached. It is the cheapest correction available, because it
costs nothing now and prevents four systems being stubbed at the wrong altitude.

### Terminology

Ben said **governing body**, not "nation". Kept as written in this item because it is the more
honest word for what is meant — the entity that governs, whatever the generated world ends up
calling it — and because Io's own naming rule (io-standing-rules § Terms & docs, same day) says
Earth's institutional vocabulary is analogy, not content. `GLOSSARY.md` should settle whether
"nation" stays the canonical term when this lands; it is not settled here.

### Still not now

Authority propagation (CONCEPT.md, SYSTEMS.md) still waits for the work, per the authority
time-slice. This section states the direction and the reason; it does not licence editing the
identity statement in CONCEPT.md ahead of the pivot.

## 2026-08-04 — corrections (dated notes, no retroactive rewrite)

1. **Nation count.** The 2026-07-04 text above says "the 14 generated Voronoi nations" four times. That count is stale: nation generation changed on 2026-07-30 and the generator now produces roughly 43. The identity claim is unaffected — the player is *one of the generated nations*, whatever their number — but read every "14" above as "the generated nations (~43 as of 2026-07-30)".
2. **Authority propagation has partially happened.** Ben instructed closing the pivot docs ahead of landing (2026-08-04, resolving NR-045's question): CONCEPT.md, SYSTEMS.md and GLOSSARY.md now state the governing-body aim as forward-looking and clearly unlanded (NR-053 records the shape chosen). The "Do NOT edit these now" lines above are therefore superseded for those three docs; full propagation in the governing body's own voice still waits for the work.
3. **Versioned (Ben, 2026-08-04, resolving NR-045).** The pivot takes its own minor: version goal **v0.3.0**, after the v0.2.0 AI opponent and before the political layer, which shifts to v0.4.0. Sequence reason recorded in ROADMAP: the AI opponent proves the game plays before the pivot changes who plays it, and politics needs the governing actor to exist first. Priority A stands.

## Update 2026-08-07 (military design session)

The owed "new conflict/military design item" named in this item’s promotion costs is now FILED as BL-315 (governing-body conflict spine), per Ben’s ruling. Bounded by the Sprint-2 precedent: specify against nation identity, never against derivation.

## 2026-08-10 — REWRITE (Sprint 8, superseding the governing-body framing)

**Status: this section supersedes every "governing body" reference above; the 2026-07-04 and
2026-08-03/04/07 sections are kept for their record of HOW the pivot was reached, not as the
current design. Read this section first.**

Ben, 2026-08-10, the refocus that produced this rewrite: *"Let's place the player as a national
private militia, which uses private companies to build equipment for space. So the flavour of
trading is initially coloured directly with military use, and space equipment."* Recorded in full
as NR-120. Three rulings were taken with Ben before this rewrite (NR-120 § rulings): the militia
**replaces** the governing body rather than reading as an early form of it; Sprint 8 settles this
on paper before anything is built against it; BL-340 (processing roster) moves to the new
Procurement minor so the goods exist before the flavour is claimed.

### What the militia is

A **national private militia**: armed, chartered by and loyal to one nation, but structurally
**private** — it holds property, contracts, and a treasury the way today's corporation does, and
it is not the nation's government. It has no legislature and no ministry of science. Its agency
runs through two things: **what it can field**, and **what it must answer to**.

This is a narrower, sharper actor than "governing body". A governing body is a whole state
apparatus that legislates, taxes, researches and commands force — that framing made law, policy
and science the player's *instruments*. A militia is a **client of the state**, not the state:
laws bind it, policy constrains where it may operate, and technology is mostly something it
*buys the output of* rather than commissions. Its own instrument is narrower and more concrete —
**procurement** — which is also why it is easier to build a legible interface for.

### The three calls this rewrite makes (resolving NR-120's still-open questions)

**1. Is the militia one of the ~43 generated nations, or attached to one?**
**Attached to one.** The player-nation call from 2026-07-04 (settled call 1, below) is
**superseded**: the player is no longer *itself* one of NATION_GENERATION.md's ~43 nations. It is
a new entity type — the private militia — that carries a `home_nation` reference into one of the
43. This keeps nation generation, the settlement history (BL-218), and the ~43-nation background
mass **completely untouched**; it adds one new actor type rather than redefining an existing one.
Symmetry (CONCEPT.md § Symmetrical rules) is preserved differently than the 2026-07-04 call
assumed: instead of every AI nation running the same governing-body layer, every nation may
sponsor / license zero or more AI-run militias that run the same militia layer the player does —
the nation itself stays the background political entity BL-218 already produces.
*Consequence for BL-054's residual (the runtime nation actor, closed 2026-08-07): it is NOT
respecified as a militia. Nations stay background; militias are the new playable/AI-contestable
layer above them.*

**2. Does the shared treasury survive?**
**No.** The 2026-07-04 "tight/shared treasury (prototype-of-1)" call is **retracted**. Private
companies under the refocus are **counterparties**: they quote a price, name a lead time, and can
refuse. That is incompatible with sharing a wallet with the buyer. The militia holds its **own**
treasury — funded by (a) a subsidy/mandate from its home nation (the nation's reason to charter a
private militia rather than run a standing army itself — cheaper, deniable, or both, a question
for CONCEPT.md's lore layer, not this item) and (b) whatever operating revenue the prototype
scopes in (today: none beyond the mandate, at prototype-of-1; a licensing or protection-contract
revenue model is a later item, not invented here). The chartered corporation of the 2026-07-04
design **stops existing as a coupled entity** — companies are now *N* independent counterparties
on the open market, exactly as any other market participant, not a linked economic arm. This is
the single largest mechanical change of the rewrite: it turns one internal transfer (nation →
governing body → chartered corp, all one ledger) into a **real negotiation** (militia treasury →
company, at a price the company sets and can refuse).

**3. What replaces the retired v0.1.x design test?**
The old test — *"does this system reach military as well as economic outcomes?"* — assumed an
actor with legislative reach. Replacement, matched to what the militia actually has:

> **Does this system change what the militia can FIELD, or what it must ANSWER TO?**

*Field* covers procurement, unit rosters, materiel, supply — the militia's positive capability.
*Answer to* covers law, policy, nation-relations, embargo — the conditions imposed on it from
outside, which it navigates rather than authors. A system that fails both — that only ever changes
a corporate cost line with no bearing on either axis — is still being designed for the player
being pivoted away from. This is the band's new litmus; apply it wherever the retired test was
cited (ROADMAP.md § v0.1.x, this item's own 2026-08-03 section below).

### What does NOT change

- **Asset-based existence** (CONCEPT.md) still holds — the militia persists as long as it holds
  any asset, and total elimination still requires its base(s) destroyed.
- **The v0.0.x economy loop underneath is unaffected in mechanism** — markets, price resolution,
  supply/demand — only the identity of the buyer changes, and the fact that its supplier is now an
  independent agent rather than itself.
- **Nation generation, settlement history, and the ~43-nation political background** (BL-218) are
  untouched; see call 1 above.
- **Symmetry** (CONCEPT.md § Symmetrical rules) still applies: every AI-run militia is chartered by
  a background nation and runs the same layer the player does.
- **The conflict spine's shape** (BL-315) is unaffected by this rewrite's mechanics, only by its
  title and the actor it is written for — see BL-315's own 2026-08-10 update.

### Scope this rewrite adds (the new promotion cost)

- **The procurement/contract seam** — counterparty, price, lead time, refusal — filed as
  **BL-350**, since nothing in the backlog covered the militia buying from an independent company
  before this rewrite.
- **A militia entity type** in the data model, distinct from both "corporation" and "nation" —
  holds a treasury, a `home_nation` reference, fielded units, and the assets a corporation held
  before it. The existing chartered-corp code is the closest analogue and the natural starting
  point for this entity's shape, not a template to inherit wholesale (it drops the shared-treasury
  coupling this rewrite retracted).
- **BL-315's re-title** to drop "governing-body" and state what it now is: the militia's conflict
  spine, still the item that turns `resolve_battle` into a campaign mechanic.

### Authority propagation (dated notes only, per the time-slice)

CONCEPT.md, SYSTEMS.md and GLOSSARY.md were already opened to the governing-body framing on
2026-08-04 (NR-053) ahead of the pivot landing — Ben's own instruction at the time. They now state
something this rewrite supersedes. Corrected here as **dated notes inline**, not a silent rewrite:
a second speculative rewrite of the identity statement in six days is exactly the churn the
authority time-slice exists to prevent. Full propagation in the militia's own voice still waits
for the work to land.

### Still open (Ben's to rule on, not resolved by this rewrite)

- The home nation's actual REASON to charter a private militia rather than field its own standing
  army — deniability, cost, historical precedent from the settlement ladder — is lore, not
  mechanism, and is not settled here.
- Whether a player can ever hold more than one militia, or switch which nation charters it, is out
  of scope for the prototype-of-1 and not addressed.
- The exact shape of the militia's non-mandate revenue (contract income, requisition, plunder) is
  left for BL-350 or a later item — this rewrite states only that the mandate is the prototype's
  funding floor.

items.title: Markets hold a resource stockpile; construction draws from / is gated on the local market stock
items.summary: Idea (2026-07-04, Ben): building materials must be a real, visible constraint sourced from the MARKET, not the corp's private pool. Today construction checks the corp's `corp_body_pools` on the body (construct_building → insufficient_materials) and markets carry only supply/demand/price — no physical resource stockpile. The one open thing was WHEN: it runs at the CLOSE of v0.1.1 as that minor acceptance pass, because BL-265 (disclosure controls), BL-266 (selection always open) and BL-229 (building selection) all change the surfaces every story walks, so walking first means recording friction against a UI about to change and paying for the review twice. items.design:
**Status:** design-owed — captured 2026-07-04 (Ben). A review pass, not a feature.

### The idea
Evaluate the UX by **user story**, not by feature list. For each core player goal, write the story and walk it through the real UI, noting every point of friction. The Selection-element redesign (BL-093) came from exactly this lens ('what's my move here?') and is the template for the kind of reframe this produces.

### Candidate stories (starting set — expand at promotion)
- **Orient:** as the player, on load I want to know *who I am and where I am* (start framing / BL-085) and *what I could do next*.
- **Find opportunity:** I want to see *where to grow* at a glance without arming build mode (Opportunity/Industry lenses, BL-086).
- **Build:** I want to pick a tile, see *what I can build, what it costs (budget + materials), and why not* (BL-071/BL-044/BL-095), and do it in a few clicks.
- **Run my economy:** I want to know *if a building is profitable* and *whether I can afford things / my runway* (BL-074/BL-072/BL-073) without hunting across ledgers.
- **Expand:** I want to *survey a new body* and judge if it's worth the cost/ETA (BL-067).
- **Read the competition:** I want to *infer what rivals are doing* from public signals (BL-068/BL-089) — markets, activity, presence.
- **Trade:** I want to see *where my goods flow* and where demand is (BL-088/BL-089, market/scarcity lenses).

### Output
A prioritised list of concrete UX fixes/reframes — most likely small (labels, ordering, an affordance moved into reach, a dead-end given a next step), some feeding or superseding existing items (e.g. BL-082 construction-panel occlusion, BL-081 ledger legibility). File the findings as their own items or a batch; this item is the *review*, its children are the work.

### Method
Best run as an advisor+Ben session walking the live app story by story (the headless walkthrough + captures ground it), or a structured heuristic pass. Proportional — the deliverable is the ranked friction list, not a rewrite. Authority `docs/ui/LAYOUT.md` for any shell-level change; per-surface docs for the rest.

### Substrate (2026-07-05) — the artifact this review consumes now exists.
The user-story catalogue is built: `docs/development/user_stories.json` (canonical) + `USER_STORIES.md` (readable view). Legacy-feature pass (2026-07-05) covers 12 stories across all seven prototype clusters (orient/find/build/operate/expand/trade/read-rivals), every story requirement-linked to req/requirements.json brief slugs — so each is a walkable, testable acceptance path. This item is the REVIEW; the catalogue is the ARTIFACT. Run the walkthrough against the catalogue rather than re-deriving the story set; findings accrete onto each story's `friction` field. New/expanded stories are authored in `user_stories.json`, not here. See CLAUDE.md § Documents (user_stories) and § Source of truth (Player-intent coverage).

## SETTLED 2026-08-02 — the method was already settled; what was missing is WHEN to run it

This is a **review activity**, not a feature, and almost everything it needs was settled by the
2026-07-05 substrate note: the artifact exists (`user_stories.json`, 12 stories across all seven
prototype clusters, each requirement-linked), the method is stated (walk the live app story by
story), and the output is defined (a ranked friction list whose findings become child items).

**The pipeline is proven, not hypothetical.** BL-175 (Supply lens legibility) came out of this
review's US-009 walkthrough and was settled today as two concrete slices. That is the item
working exactly as designed — a story walked, a friction found, an item filed, a design settled.

### The one open thing: run it AFTER the v0.1.1 UI batch, not before

Settled: **this review runs at the close of v0.1.1, as that minor's acceptance pass.**

Three items settled today change the surfaces every story walks through:

- **BL-265** — two disclosure controls, canvas-bounded takeover, right-gutter alignment.
- **BL-266** — the Selection band never closes and rests on the player's corporation.
- **BL-229** — the building Selection element reshaped to three columns.

Walking the stories before those land means recording friction against a UI that is about to
change, and re-walking afterward — the review's cost paid twice for one result. Walking them
after means the review is also the check that the batch actually improved the flows, which is a
second job for the same effort.

**"Orient" is the story most affected**, since BL-266 changes what a player sees before they
have selected anything — which is literally the opening frame.

### Method, confirmed and bounded

- Run as an **advisor + Ben session against the live app** (the standing rule for visual
  judgement), story by story, grounded by the headless walkthrough and captures.
- **Findings accrete onto each story's `friction` field** in `user_stories.json`; new or
  expanded stories are authored there, never in this item.
- **Proportional** — the deliverable is the ranked list. Fixes are child items, and this item
  does not implement any of them.
- **A story that no surface serves is a gap; a feature no story needs is scope to justify.**
  Both directions get reported, not just the first.

**Version goal set to v0.1.1** (was unset), reflecting that it closes that minor rather than
floating.

items.title: Commercial-fog proximity-glimpse peek — routing past a frontier body reveals it (deterministic)
items.summary: Deferred at BL-089's landing (recorded in its resolution): the deterministic proximity-glimpse 'peek'. When a player convoy completes a lane, sample body positions at that completion tick and mark any body within radius R of the lane segment as known_stale — a faint, decaying glimpse. Makes 'route past a frontier body to reveal it' discrete and deterministic (one sample at a discrete tick; positions are a pure function of tick — no per-frame test, no flicker, no RNG). R + freshness are headless-tuned calibration constants. BL-089 shipped the core fog (endpoint badge + corridor + Selection activity section) but this third illumination geometry was cut to land the item; captured here as its own promote-ready item. (Renumbered from BL-095 on merge to main 2026-07-05 — a cross-branch collision with main's BL-095 market-stockpile item.) DEFERRAL DECISION (v0.0.9 batch, 2026-07-05): assessed and HELD BACK. A faithful implementation needs either a serialised last_glimpse_tick on body_component (a save-seam change) or orbital back-computation from the mutated orbital_angle_rad — body position is NOT a pure function of tick today, contrary to the mechanic's premise, so 'sample body positions at the completion tick' cannot be reconstructed at a later render without stored state. Disproportionate determinism/serialisation risk for a polish minor; re-assess at the v0.1.0 boundary. Stays designed/promote-ready. [COMPLETE 2026-07-08 (BL-099 delivery): shipped via SAMPLE-AND-STORE, which dissolves the deferral objection. Positions ARE mutated (orbital_angle_rad, not pure in tick) as the deferral said -- so instead of reconstructing a past position, record_proximity_glimpses samples the closest-approach set ONCE at the discrete completion tick (credit_arrived_convoys, after orbits advanced for that frame, so live positions ARE the completion-tick positions) and stores the glimpse tick in world.body_last_glimpse_tick (off body_component, keeping the flat-binary layout untouched). body_activity_visibility returns known_stale for a glimpsed-but-unrouted body within glimpse_fresh_ticks_default (90), never known/visible; a body's own route outranks a glimpse; R=glimpse_radius_au_default (0.25 AU). The sample lives in supply_system.cpp (the actual completion hook -- the original files list omitted it); the renderer was NOT touched (the known_stale badge path is BL-089's, already blessed -- BL-099 only widens which bodies reach that tier). Verified: commercial_fog_harness 19/19 (10 new assertions -- geometry, tier, endpoint-exclusion, decay, route-precedence, determinism) + full CTest 19/19 (determinism intact); on-canvas by-eye via scripts/verify/proximity_glimpse.lua before/after. Authority propagated to DISCOVERY.md. Golden bless owed on the Linux box.]

items.design:
**Status:** designed but BLOCKED — settled from the 2026-07-05 health sweep (quick-win #7). *Still blocked, but not for the reason first written: see the 2026-08-10 note at the foot of this entry, refreshed 2026-08-12.*

**Design:** reserve a fixed leading header on every flat-binary snapshot — a **magic uint32** (e.g. 'IOSV') plus a monotonically-incremented **format-version uint32** — written first and checked on load. A mismatched magic or version fails the load with a clear error rather than reading a struct-layout mismatch as garbage. Bump the version whenever a serialised struct's layout changes.

**BLOCKED** *(reason corrected 2026-08-12, NR-157)*: the original wording — "no flat-binary serialiser exists in `world/*` yet (grep finds only PNG `fwrite` in `core/*`), so there is nothing to version" — is **stale and should not be quoted**. THREE flat-binary streams now exist and every one already carries this item's magic + version header: `history_log` (`IOHL`), `order_book` (`IOOB`) and `procurement` (`IOPC`, BL-350). The 2026-08-10 note below says two, which was true that day. What is still missing is the **world-snapshot serialiser** — the whole-world save this item was always about — and no backlog item covers writing it. So the item remains blocked, on a narrower and more accurate thing, and it is no longer "the FIRST thing to add": the convention is already established by two working precedents, and this is its application to the world save.

**Shipped now under the 2026-07-05 batch:** the doc-truthfulness fix only — softening TECH_FOUNDATIONS' present-tense 'is serialised' / 'are written and read' claims to future tense so the invariant is not stated as already built.

**Note:** the serialisation implementation itself is not yet a backlog item — file one before promoting this.

**Shipped 2026-07-05 (health-sweep batch):** the doc-truthfulness half only — TECH_FOUNDATIONS § Save model / Serialisation softened from present tense ('is serialised' / 'are written and read') to future, with a forward-reference to this item's magic+version header. The item PROPER (the header) stays `designed` + blocked on the serialiser landing. **Authority:** docs/tech/TECH_FOUNDATIONS.md.

## 2026-08-10 - the BLOCKED reason is STALE (NR-157)

The status above says "no flat-binary serialiser exists in `world/*` yet (grep finds only PNG
`fwrite` in `core/*`), so there is nothing to version". That was true when written. It is not now.

**Two flat-binary streams exist**, and both already carry exactly the magic + version header this
item specifies, each citing this item as the reason:

- `src/world/history_log.{hpp,cpp}` - magic `IOHL`, `history_log_version`.
- `src/world/order_book.{hpp,cpp}` - magic `IOOB`, `order_book_version` (BL-293, landed 2026-08-10).

Both reject a mismatched magic or version rather than reinterpreting the bytes, which is this
item's design realised in miniature. What remains owed is therefore the **world-snapshot** header -
the whole-world save this item was originally about - not the first-ever one, and not the
convention, which is now established by two working precedents.

**Consequence for BL-340**, which reverses an earlier reading: `read_order_book` rejects a resource
byte that does not name a known `resource_type`. Widening the enum therefore moves a validation
boundary inside a **shipped serialised stream**, so the version bump BL-340 needs is real work
rather than a hypothetical. Still not a blocker for it; just no longer free.

items.title: Revisit real market inventory vs derived-from-supply stock (post-optimization)
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-07 from the economy design session. BL-095 settled on DERIVED-from-supply market stock (a rolling throughput figure) for calculation simplicity, deferring a real persistent per-resource inventory. Ben: revisit once we have had a moment to work on optimisation and efficiency of the program. A real inventory is the cleaner substrate for competition and for a future RUNTIME market split/merge, at the cost of a serialized field on the flat-binary seam + tick accounting. SETTLED 2026-08-02: YES to a real persistent per-resource inventory. BL-263 (markets become runtime simulation state) both weakened the objection — the flat-binary seam is already being opened for markets that did not exist at generation — and strengthened the case, since an outpost market clearing against remote demand has stock in transit vs on hand, which a derived-from-supply figure cannot represent, and dormancy is inventory nobody clears rather than zero supply. The optimization gate stands but is a TIMING gate, not a decision gate. Now sequenced after BL-263.
items.design:
Post-optimization revisit of the BL-095 stock model. Decide whether markets should hold a **real persistent per-resource inventory** (fills from production + nation capacity, drains to consumption + construction) rather than a derived-from-recent-supply figure. Trade-off: a real inventory is the cleanest substrate for "greedy actors compete for stock" and for runtime market split/merge (BL-132), but adds a serialized array to the flat-binary seam and deterministic tick accounting. Gate: only worth doing after a general optimization/efficiency pass. `requires` BL-095. Authority → PRODUCTION.md on landing.

## SETTLED 2026-08-02 — yes, a real inventory. The gate is about TIMING, not the decision.

**Decision: markets hold a real persistent per-resource inventory.** The item framed this as an
open trade-off; BL-263 (settled the same day) has largely resolved it.

**The main objection weakened.** "Adds a serialised array to the flat-binary seam" was the cost
against. BL-263 makes markets *runtime simulation state* — created mid-campaign, persisted,
going dormant — so the save format is already gaining a count-prefixed run of markets that did
not exist at generation. Adding inventory to a record already being opened is a much smaller
change than adding it to a fixed generation artifact.

**The case for got stronger.** A real inventory is the substrate for "greedy actors compete for
stock", and BL-263's outpost markets need exactly that: a market clearing against remote demand
has stock in transit and stock on hand, which a derived-from-recent-supply figure cannot
represent. A derived figure also cannot express dormancy honestly — a dormant market has
inventory nobody is clearing, not zero supply.

**The gate stands, but it is a timing gate.** "Only worth doing after a general
optimization/efficiency pass" remains true — this adds per-tick accounting on a hot path. What
is settled is *which way it goes* when the gate opens, so the question is not re-litigated.

**Sequence after BL-263**, not before: building inventory into a fixed generation-time market
set, then reworking it when markets become runtime state, is doing it twice.

**Determinism.** Inventory accounting is fixed-point, and fills/drains within a tick must
combine order-independently — the same summed-rate rule BL-155 settled for law margin
modifiers, for the same reason.
items.resolution: 2026-08-11 — complete. Real persistent per-resource inventory (market_component.inventory, real state, not reset per tick) replaces the derived-from-recent-supply proxy on the BUY side only — the sell side stays unconditional (unchanged, per MARKETS.md's existing invariant). FILLS from real corp sales only (auto-surplus + standing sell orders, tallied separately from mc.supply so the BL-078 substrate's abstract supply cannot inflate real stock). DRAINS during production (run_processing) and construction (run_construction), both of which run BEFORE clear_markets in the same tick, against whatever stock survived prior ticks' sales. run_processing's old "a market body always runs a full batch, auto-buying any shortfall unconditionally" special case is retired: coverage is now (pool + market inventory) / need per input, and the two-threshold partial-run model governs uniformly whether or not a market backs the body — PRODUCTION.md's stale 2026-07-31 note corrected accordingly. run_construction (BL-095's pacing rate) swaps its "recent supply" proxy for the real field and now actually drains it. Determinism: both consumers draw the SAME live inventory in the existing fixed tick order (construction, then production), and a processor's run fraction is bounded by the coverage-min across every input by construction, so total draw in one tick can never exceed what was on hand — no proportional-fairness math needed, no double-spend. New market_inventory_harness (14/14 PASS): idle with nothing available, full batch from ample market stock with an exact drain check, pool-then-market draw order, the two-threshold model applying on a market body, real fill from a real sale (not substrate), and construction's own gate reading/draining the same field. Found and fixed a real, serious, pre-existing bug while diagnosing an unrelated crash in pregame_balance_harness: BL-368 added three resource_type values but never registered their Lua names in recipe_registry.cpp's resource_from_name table, so the actual game has been crashing on startup (unhandled std::runtime_error loading recipes.lua) since BL-368 landed earlier this session — fixed by adding the three missing table entries. Also added a top-level try/catch to pregame_balance_harness's main() (kept, not reverted) so a future Lua-load error surfaces its message instead of a bare abort(). Fixed three existing harnesses whose hand-built fixtures assumed the retired unconditional-auto-buy model (econ_harness, resource_chain_harness, construction_gate_harness) by seeding mc.inventory alongside their existing mc.supply/pool seeding — the fixture intent (a market with real stock) is unchanged, only the field that carries it. Full ProjectIo build clean; the complete harness suite (15 harnesses) rerun clean from a FRESH rebuild (not stale exes — a mistake caught and corrected twice this session, see NR-169). pregame_balance_harness (the real generated world, 80-tick warm start) confirmed sane: climbs cleanly to a ~108k plateau, no crash, no negative balance, all 5 dynamism/determinism assertions pass. ai_skill_harness moved from 8 to 9 golden-band failures (one new: seed 4 net-worth min) — attributable and expected, a real economy change, not instability; recorded in NR-169 rather than re-blessed. docs/economy/MARKETS.md gains § Real market inventory and corrects the Known-limitations entry; docs/economy/PRODUCTION.md's stale "thresholds bypassed on market bodies" note corrected. BL-365 (the keystone) is now unblocked.

items.title: Player-driven market destruction (the only runtime market change)
