items.title: Territorial fragmentation, measured — reopened from BL-054: assert exclaves actually emerge rather than trusting the argument that chose the expensive path
items.summary: Ben, 2026-08-03 (NR-036): BL-054's territorial-fragmentation half is REOPENED as its own measurable item rather than being counted complete on the strength of BL-218's design argument. That argument — 'a real settlement sim produces exclaves for free; a growth front that crosses a strait and stalls leaves an exclave without anyone authoring one' — is what chose the expensive option over the cheap one. It has never been measured. Until it is, BL-054's territorial half is not complete.

(1) Re-run and re-bless the GCC golden set on the next Linux session — only the MSVC set was re-blessed, so the two platforms are currently drifting apart. (2) Tag history-ladder lines with their own `chain_stage` so H4 can filter on a field rather than text-match a line; text-matching is exactly the fragility that assertion had to be narrowed around.

items.title: Logistics goods — extend resource_type with grain, fodder, salt, transport capacity, charcoal, iron blooms, bullion, and a placeholder endemic-luxury slot (enum + base-price wiring only)
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-04 from a Ben brainstorm about the 0 A.D. sandbox (Project-Rival, BL-271 era −1 proving ground): what other resources does a diverse, realistic logistics system need beyond food/wood/stone/metal? The answer organised around three axes rather than a longer stock list — per-tick flows (grain, fodder, water, salt), carrying capacity as a held resource (transport_capacity), and value density (charcoal, iron blooms, bullion, an endemic-luxury slot). Ben decided (2026-08-04) to ship these as a permanent extension of the shared resource_type enum — not a sandbox-local roster as first drafted — so resource_count moves from 23 to 31 and this IS a save-format retrofit (RESOURCES.md § Prototype scope). This item lands the enum values, name-lookup wiring, and authored placeholder base prices only; no consumption, transport-range cap, salt shelf-life gate, or bullion purchase mechanic reads them yet.

items.title: Verify tier rebuilds the world layer once per harness (44x duplication)
Four harnesses fail in Release and nobody noticed, because the default build dir is Debug
Make the sky events causal: a nearby supernova as a real mass-extinction driver
items.design:
DEFERRED DELIBERATELY. Ben, 2026-08-04: "just flavor, keep a deferred item with your thoughts
for if I decide to add more challenging aspects." The star map and its supernova/quasar lines
landed as pure narration — no gate reads them, no endowment moves. This item is the version
with teeth, recorded now while the reasoning is in hand.

WHY IT IS TEMPTING. A nearby supernova is a real extinction mechanism, and it happens to be
the one kind of catastrophe this model has no way to express. Every existing failure in the
chain is a property of the world itself — too little heat, too much ocean, the wrong oxygen
timing. All of them are things the player chose in the wizard, however indirectly. A supernova
is the first cause that is NOT about the world: it arrives from outside, it is nobody's fault,
and it is the only mechanism in the design that could make two otherwise-identical worlds
diverge. That is worth something narratively that no amount of knob-tuning provides.

THE MECHANISM, IF BUILT. Ozone is already modelled — ozone_du() in planetology.cpp, a lookup
against O2 as a fraction of present level, used by the S7 land-colonisation gate at a 60 DU
threshold. A supernova within ~10 parsecs strips a large fraction of the ozone column for
years to decades. So the hook is exact and already present: temporarily depress the ozone
column at the moment the light arrives, and let the EXISTING S7 gate do the work. If the world
had only just cleared 60 DU, it loses its land biosphere and becomes a Graveyard; if it was
comfortably above, it survives with a scar in the biography. No new gate, no new archetype —
the graveyard mechanic (peak vs current life_stage) already models exactly this outcome, where
the coal survives and the forests do not.

BL-217's checkpoint machinery is the natural home: a checkpoint_record at chain_stage::green
with branch_taken "supernova at N pc - ozone stripped" and viability_result set by whether the
biosphere held. That gets it into the replayable branch history for free.

WHAT MAKES IT HARD, AND WHY IT IS NOT DEFAULT-ON.
1. The star map is FIXED and the campaign is not. A supernova at a fixed sky position is at a
   fixed DISTANCE only if every campaign system sits in the same place in the galaxy, which is
   currently unstated. Either the campaign system gets a galactic position (new state), or the
   distance is drawn per campaign and the fixed map becomes a fixed DIRECTION with a variable
   range. The second is cheaper and probably right, but it means the sky lies slightly: the
   same remnant is 8 pc away in one campaign and 300 in another.
2. It reintroduces exactly the failure mode this session spent a day measuring away. A world
   can now fail for a reason no wizard preference predicts, which is thrilling once and
   infuriating on the fourth reroll. It wants a rate, and the rate wants measuring — the
   earthlike battery (planetology_sweep C1, earthlike_tile_census) is the instrument, and the
   question is what fraction of campaigns should lose their biosphere this way. My guess is
   low single digits, and that it should never fire on the homeworld before civilisation
   unless Ben wants Era -1 to be genuinely dangerous.
3. The homeworld floor would have to decide whether it cares. homeworld_viability rejects
   non-Cradles, so a supernova-killed homeworld is simply rerolled and the player never sees
   it — the drama lands only on NON-homeworld bodies, or if the floor gains an exception. The
   more interesting version is the latter: a Graveyard homeworld the player is told about and
   must live with. That is a much bigger design decision than the mechanism.

CHEAPER MIDDLE GROUND, if the full version is too much: let the supernova fire on non-homeworld
bodies only. Cinder, Selene and Pallas have no biosphere to lose, so today it would be inert —
but it becomes live the moment the body count grows (PLANETOLOGY.md Open call 2), and it gives
the sky something to do without ever costing the player their own world.

SEE ALSO: the quasar is deliberately excluded from all of this. It has been shining the whole
time, which is exactly why it makes a good fixed landmark and a bad event.

items.title: The nation and city name banks are Latin/European, and ignore the culture phonology creeds already rolls
world_audit fails, so the tile census cannot be re-measured and TILES.md stays stale
The Economy panel is drawn every frame but has no door — no nav slot, no action entry
Three order-book presses exist in the dictionary but have no corp_command verb, so no text player can trade
items.design:
FOUND BY THE DOCUMENTATION AUDIT (2026-08-04), and independently logged in Project-Rival's own
findings doc as its ranked gap #4 — so this is the second time it has surfaced.

THE GAP. `ACTIONS.json` carries gameplay entries for `place_sell_order`, `remove_sell_order` and
`set_workforce_auto`. None has a `corp_verb`; the enum in corp_command.hpp is eight wide and holds
none of them. So they are player-only presses: a text-driven player can READ the order book and
can be told what the press MEANS, but has no way to issue it.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THREE MISSING VERBS. Standing sell orders with a floor price are how a
corporation governs the release of its own stock rather than dumping at the resolved price
(SYSTEMS.md § Trade). An agent that cannot place one is not playing the economy; it is watching
it. The word interface is v0.1.1's theme and this is the hole in its write leg.

ALSO FIX THE OVERCLAIM: ACTIONS.md's preamble says pairing the three legs gives an LLM "the full
word interface". Until this lands that is false, and it is the one line in the dictionary most
likely to mislead. Either close the gap or state the narrowing — closing it is better.

SEQUENCING: the gameplay family is TRANSCRIBED from corp_command.hpp, never authored. So the seam
changes first, then the dictionary is re-transcribed and the mirror re-rendered.

## Scope correction 2026-08-07 — stopped before coding

The item assumes the three presses only lack a verb. They lack a PLACE TO PUT ONE. `sell_order` is defined in world/components.hpp:368 but stored in ui_state.hpp:273 and handed to `clear_markets` by the caller (app.cpp:566); the world has no order book. A corp_verb mutates `world&`, so there is nothing to mutate.

Also found: no serialisation path touches sell_order or buy_order, so standing orders appear not to survive save/load — a defect independent of this item.

And the gate: corp_verb is the seam corp_ai.cpp drives every rival corp through. The standing rules enumerate what that scored-utility layer may do and TRADING IS NOT ON THE LIST. Adding place_sell_order widens the AI's reach as a side effect. That is Ben's call, so this stopped at the finding. See the review entry for the three options.

Difficulty and files as filed are both understated: this is Full-mode, save-format-touching work, not a transcription follow-up.
items.resolution:
LANDED 2026-08-08, at the size the 2026-08-07 scope correction found rather than the size it was filed at.

Ben's ruling (NR-083): "Order book needs to be a background process, the AI must be able to trade as a player does."
The player-only fence proposed alongside it was explicitly rejected.

WHAT LANDED.
1. The order book is world state. `world::sell_orders` / `buy_orders` / `next_order_id`; orders carry a stable
   `id` so removal names identity rather than an index. It lived on ui_state, which cost three things at once:
   clearing was UI-driven, a corp_verb had nothing to mutate, and standing orders were outside the save seam.
2. It is serialised. `order_book.{hpp,cpp}` - magic IOOB + version, the second flat-binary stream in world/*
   after history_log, refusing a bad stream rather than reinterpreting it.
3. Matching is a background process. `clear_markets` DROPPED both order-list parameters and reads the world;
   a headless tick now sells a standing order with nobody handing it over.
4. Three verbs joined the seam: place_sell_order, remove_sell_order, set_workforce_auto (enum now 11 wide,
   append-only). The Market Ledger's buttons queue corp_commands that app::render applies through
   apply_corp_command - the player's press and the AI's command are one implementation, not two that agree.
5. Rival corps trade, per the ruling. Conservative first cut: surplus past a hold threshold, half the excess,
   floored at the market's rarity price, scored at the floor. Tunables in corp_ai_params. See NR-087.
6. The standing rules were amended - the rival-corp exception's verb list did not include trading, and Ben's
   ruling widens it. Flagged explicitly rather than slipped in: NR-085.

FOUND ALONG THE WAY. `set_workforce` never cleared `workforce_auto`, though ACTIONS.json has always said it did

items.title: diverging_colour and icons::unit have zero call sites
A components.hpp comment cites BL-287 to BL-290 for logistics-goods follow-ons that were never filed
Ancient tech ladder — the 0 CE -> 1960 tech spine (bands x domains x diffusion classes) that the Era -1 sim and the era-keyed rosters key off
items.design:
MOCKED UP 2026-08-04 (Ben: 'mock up an ancient tech tree as a basis; consider the major advancements from 0 AD, and what differences are realistic by 1960 AD'). The full mockup lives in docs/research/ANCIENT_TECH_LADDER.md — this item is its tracked home; the design conversation happens against that doc.

SHAPE, in one paragraph: six bands (T1 Classical -> T6 Machine Age) x seven domains (Agriculture / Materials / Energy / Transport / Institutions / Military / Medicine), ~60 load-bearing nodes with prereqs, endowment gates over settlement_state (ore_q / fuel / arable / coastal / grassland), and a three-class DIFFUSION axis (artifact / practice / capacity) that generates the realistic 1960 inequality: knowledge spread ~0 bands, capacity spread 3-4 bands, military-artifact spread 1-2 bands. Honours the BL-274 stance in full — derived availability, never a player-facing research tree; the tree structure is data the BL-271 year-tick sim evaluates.

RELATION TO SIBLINGS: BL-271 (Era -1 sim) is the consumer of the acquisition model (invention at the frontier / practice diffusion by contact / artifact flow by trade / capacity regression on rupture). BL-274 (era-keyed rosters) reads the Military band boundaries plus the capacity-vs-artifact split (what a nation FIELDS vs what it can REPLACE under blockade). BL-273 (province demography) reads the Medicine and Agriculture bands. The T6 exit hands off to scripts/tech_tree.lua (BL-087) at the campaign epoch.

OPEN QUESTIONS (in the doc, section-final): band-count reconciliation with BL-274 four-band lean; per-domain capacity + artifact-access state representation; C++ table vs Lua data home; whether the player ever sees a 1960 codex rendering. NR-054 / NR-055 record the two calls taken on Ben behalf.

GEOMETRY SETTLED (2026-08-04, follow-up session, Ben): the constellation — see the docs § Geometry (rings = bands, sectors = domains, entry = endowment, travel-OR / meaning-AND, keystone exclusion via windows, tech fog). This overturns BL-087 Q1 (recorded there and in ERA1_TECH_LANDSCAPE.md § Q1). NEXT STEP, per Ben: test how much detail makes the game FUN against worked examples — the docs § Density test carries one slice (the steam transition) at three grains; recommendation medium (~100-150 nodes web-wide, fine grain only around keystones); NR-056 holds the call.

SECOND DENSITY SLICE (2026-08-04, same day): Institutions at medium grain, as the contrast test — practice-class nodes, an ideological keystone (Sovereign Doctrine: Chartered Capital vs Command Estate — HISTORY.md Stage 3 turned into a choice, creed-picked for AI nations), and three invented VERTEX QUESTS (The Enforceable Promise / The Disciplined Sovereign / The Lettered Public). New geometry rule recorded same day: VERTICES ARE QUESTS — the BL-087 gate=quest=tech object placed at ring crossings, capstone carrying the economic conditions, completion opening the next ring region in that sector.

GRAIN SETTLED: MEDIUM (Ben, 2026-08-04 — NR-056 resolved), and the RING-1-TO-2 NEIGHBOURHOOD is worked in full at that grain (docs § The ring-1-to-2 neighbourhood): 19 techs + 5 vertex quests (The Common Forge / The Tireless Wheel / All Roads Home / The Written Ledger / The Fed Village) + the GRANARY DOCTRINE keystone (Temple Stores vs Open Granaries — the campaigns markets-not-command premise made a ring-1 choice) + 2 roster regimes = 27 objects (count corrected 2026-08-04 against the BL-307 data store), extrapolating to ~130-150 web-wide. New rule adopted with the pass: the SPARSE-SECTOR RULE — a sector earns a vertex quest only at a genuine capability regime (Military crosses on the BL-274 roster turnover, Medicine on a plain edge). Visual sketch generated (scratchpad, session artifact).

INDUSTRIAL NEIGHBOURHOOD (2026-08-05, Ben: 'another pre-game tech tree centred around the industrial revolution, to go alongside the pre-game early Civilisation tech tree'): the second complete region, worked at the settled medium grain in the doc's SS The industrial neighbourhood — rings T4-T5 and the T4/T5 crossings. Scope read as a second worked REGION of the one shared web, not a second web (NR-063). Content: 7 new techs (Coal Haulage & Urban Fuel, Patent Grants, Preventive Inoculation, High-Pressure & Compound Engines, Framed Construction & Cement, Soil Chemistry & Fertiliser Trade, General Incorporation), 4 new vertex quests (The Unwearied Fire / The Cheap Ton / The Scheduled World / The Freed Hands, joining the existing Disciplined Sovereign), and 2 new keystones — LABOUR DOCTRINE (Cleared Holdings vs Smallholder Tenure; the human price of the divergence, feeding BL-273 demography) and WORKS DOCTRINE (State Arsenal vs Private Works; who owns the heavy plant, and therefore the terms a player corporation operates on in 1960). Fuel Doctrine relocated ring T5 -> T4 so The Cheap Ton can require it taken (the ring-1 interlock, repeated — now the house rule). New authoring rule: FORK COUNT SCALES WITH THE BAND'S DIVERGENCE (ring 1 carries one keystone; this region carries four). Region totals 38 objects, 13 new here; web-wide 88 objects with two of five ring-crossings worked, extrapolating to ~120-135. ladder_lint.js generalised to print one line per worked region. Open: NR-064 asks whether Works Doctrine gates corporation generation (lean: yes, file an item when this lands) and whether the region earns its own viewer tab (lean: no — the era strip means eras). EFFECTS PASS (2026-08-05, Ben: 'let's map this to real buildings and units'): every tech, regime and keystone branch in rings T4-T5 now carries an `effects` array in the store - 62 effects, modifier 19 / institution 11 / unlock 10 / upgrade 5 / reach 4 / retire 4 / access 3 / intel 3 / resource 2 / doctrine 1, at shipped 15 / designed 29 / unbuilt 18. Taxonomy authored in docs/research/TECH_EFFECTS.md under BL-156. ladder_lint.js validates the kind/status vocabulary and enforces that no object in the typed region is left untyped.

items.title: Text-only Rival harness - drive 0 A.D. through its official RL interface (zero_ad seam), replacing computer-use as the campaign mode
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-04 from the text-only SOTA sweep (NR-057). 0 A.D. ships --rl-interface (Alpha 24, official HTTP seam) driven by the in-tree zero_ad Python client: JSON scenario in, full JSON state per step, programmatic commands, exact step control, headless. The harness replaces computer-use as the campaign mode: text observations beat pixels for decision quality (BALROG, lmgame-Bench), year marks become exact ticks, and the rite gains machine-checkable conformance. Rival constraint honoured: the seam is an official engine flag - nothing patched, nothing hooked.
items.design:
## Shape (settled 2026-08-04)

Three layers, mirroring the TextStarCraft-II pattern (arXiv:2312.11865) and Io's own word-interface triple:

1. **Summarizer (read).** zero_ad JSON state -> terse situation report: holdings, hosts, rival's visible works, fog-as-gaps. This IS station 1 (Omens); Muninn's law becomes machine-checkable (report only what the JSON showed).
2. **Macro-action vocabulary (write).** The dispatch grammar - god sends soldiers to place, for purpose - compiles to grouped macro-actions (train / build / group attack-move). No unit micro. Validation with error echo + fallback; every invalid action logged as a first-class metric (BALROG practice).
3. **MCP wrapper (meaning).** A thin server mirroring Io's five tools (get_blackboard / issue_command / advance_tick / lookup_action / list_actions), so 0 A.D. play rehearses exactly the seam Io's AI opponent will use (Orak precedent: MCP as the game-agent socket).

## Constraints

- Pin Release 28; the seam is lightly-maintained research tooling. First harness task is a **conformance smoke test** against the R28 JSON schema; it gates every campaign session.
- Frontier weakness guard: carry a map summary / pathfinder-style tool in the harness rather than expecting the model to do geometry (FLE, CivRealm findings).
- Memory-as-files: the annals remain the durable memory layer (Claude-Pokemon lineage pattern); context resets against them, not against transcript.
- Lives entirely under Project-Rival/; never writes Io source.

## Re-aim (2026-08-04, same day — NR-060)

The RTS arena is retired: "0 AD" means the year, not Wildfire Games' game, and the install
was removed the day it landed. The harness re-aims at **Project Io's own word interface**:
the MCP seam (BL-278) today, the Era -1 sandbox (BL-271) with the diplomacy seam (BL-307)
as the destination board.

What survives unchanged: the three-layer shape (summarizer -> Omens; dispatch grammar ->
macro-actions; MCP as the socket), the conformance-smoke-gates-every-session rule, the
invalid-action metric, memory-as-files via the annals. What falls away: everything
zero_ad-specific (the protocol knowledge is preserved in tools/harness/smoke_test.js as a
record). The summarizer now reads the corp/nation blackboard; the grammar compiles
dispatches to corp_command / diplomacy verbs instead of RTS macros.

items.title: Era -1 diplomacy seam - nation blackboard + typed diplomacy verbs over a year-tick command queue (the word interface's nation leg)
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-04. The diplomacy system develops by play (Project-Rival method) against the Era -1 sandbox: extend the word interface with a nation-level leg - a nation blackboard plus a small typed diplomacy verb family. Verbs enter through a command queue at year-tick boundaries only, so determinism holds: seed + command log = full replay. Respects BL-277's scope guard - the deterministic strategy layer stays LLM-free; the agent sits outside the engine via MCP, same as the corp AI direction. No HTTP client, no cloud dependency inside the engine.
items.design:
## Shape (settled 2026-08-04)

- **Nation blackboard**: per-nation JSON export - holdings, hosts, treasury/manpower, standing wars, known offers - the read leg at nation grain.
- **Verb family** (final roster a design task, start small): offer_peace, demand_tribute, propose_pact, threaten. Each verb typed - preconditions, args, expected_output - and transcribed into ACTIONS.json's conventions so dictionary and seam cannot drift.
- **Command queue at year-tick boundaries.** The sim never blocks on an agent; queued verbs resolve at the next year tick, deterministically. Replay = seed + command log (the enabler for Critical State Analysis: checkpoint a decisive year, replay it many times per policy).
- **Intent-conditioning (Cicero's transferable idea).** Every negotiation message is generated from a declared planned action set; offers/acceptances carry structured machine-parseable fields (NegotiationArena pattern) wrapped in whatever prose the voice wants. Claims-vs-subsequent-actions gives a lie metric for free.
- **Small-local-model support**: AI Diplomacy (arXiv:2508.07485) showed a well-iterated textual state lets 24B local models play full-press - direct support for the no-cloud invariant.

Harness-flag territory like its parent BL-271: never in the shipped campaign path.

items.title: Diplomacy test battery - conformance, replay determinism, legality matrix, baselines and negotiation checks for the Era -1 seam
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-04. The verification battery that makes diplomacy-by-play trustworthy, all standard practice in the 2025-26 agent literature and all mapped onto house verifiers. Ordering rule: checks 1-2 run before any LLM ever touches the seam.
items.design:
## The seven checks (settled 2026-08-04)

1. **Harness conformance, pre-LLM.** A scripted policy drives the full verb set; pass = zero protocol errors. Invalid-action rate becomes a first-class per-session metric thereafter.
2. **Determinism replay.** Seed + recorded diplomacy-command log, run twice, identical world hash - a tools/verify/ harness, verifier-headless class.
3. **Legality matrix.** Every verb x precondition (peace without war, tribute above treasury) rejected deterministically with a reason echoed back - error echo + fallback keeps agent runs from wedging.
4. **Seed-start assertion.** The BL-299 great-power seed check: two majors present, opposed creeds assigned, no hegemony within N years under null diplomacy (extends BL-275 sweep metrics).
5. **Baseline calibration.** Random and scripted policies (always-refuse, tit-for-tat) run first so agent skill separates from noise (lmgame-Bench: 40% of unharnessed runs fail to beat random).
6. **Negotiation checks.** Intent-conditioning verified (message references its declared plan); structured offer/accept fields parse; lie metric (claims vs subsequent actions) recorded per campaign.
7. **Rite conformance extension.** R1-R8 carry over; text mode makes R6 (omens = what the interface showed) and R8 (evidence = seed + command log) machine-checkable, and adds R9: every issued action validated legal.

items.title: Two-great-powers seed - a sandbox world_params option: opposed strategic creeds (self-preservation vs civilising mission) in a multipolar antiquity
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-04 at Ben's request: seed the Era -1 sandbox with a multipolar origin carrying two great powers - one devoted to self-preservation (the preserving creed), one to a civilising mission (the expansionist creed). The sandbox proving ground for early logistics and military under low-friction economics. Maps one-to-one onto the Rival dossier's Rome/Han axis - as mechanism, never as names.
items.design:
## Shape (settled 2026-08-04)

- **A world_params seeding option**, not a new pass: the settlement world (BL-218) seeds two majors with opposed strategic creeds; creed lean feeds doctrine choice per BL-277's question 5.
- **Multipolar periphery preserved.** BL-224's non-hegemony invariant as tuning target: neither major absorbs the world early; the periphery stays alive as actors, not terrain.
- **Low-friction economics.** Era progression frozen - no tech ladder, one fixed roster tier (BL-274) - so the sandbox tests logistics and military, not industrialisation. Nobody invents the steam engine (Ben, 2026-08-04).
- **Periphery richness clause (Ben, 2026-08-04):** "while the focus is on how these empires change and crumble, we should not miss the richness of each other civilisation." Every generated civilisation - majors AND minors - gets full character: creeds, myths (BL-300), naming, doctrine lean, its own recorded history. Minors are civilisations in their own right, not buffer states.
- **Naming constraint** (io-standing-rules, 2026-08-03): self-preservation/civilising-mission are mechanism references; no Latin-reading or Chinese-reading phonemes, no proper nouns from Earth.

items.title: Myth & theology generation - structurally accurate myths and real veneration of old gods for every Era -1 civilisation
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-04 from Ben's steer: "make sure that we do map theology onto primitive civilisations - i.e. there is an accurate generation of myths, and real veneration of old gods." The creeds system already makes gods mechanical (war gods drive battle odds; a won war plants the victor's pantheon); this item gives every civilisation a generated theology worth planting - and makes old gods persist.
items.design:
## Intent (design-owed)

Questions the design must settle:

1. **Myth-type banks, structurally faithful.** Creation, flood/deluge, culture-hero, ancestor cult, sky-father/earth-mother pairings, syncretism-on-conquest - the STRUCTURES are the transfer from real mythology (mechanism reference); every god, hero and place name is invented per the standing naming rule.
2. **Derivation, not dice.** Per the generation rule (consequences of upstream scalars): a river-valley civilisation derives flood myths, a littoral one storm-and-sea cults, a forge-rich one smith gods - theology reads off terrain, biosphere history (BL-167 planetology outputs) and early economy.
3. **Real veneration of old gods.** Conquest plants the victor's pantheon but does NOT erase the old one: old gods persist as substrate cults, syncretise (victor's war god acquires the local storm god's epithets), or go underground - interacting with the record-burning rule (a burned record does not unmake a venerated god; the cult remembers what the chronicle lost).
4. **Consumers.** The oral-history pivot (BL-210) reads generated theology for dispatch idiom; BL-299's periphery-richness clause makes every civilisation's theology first-class, not just the two majors'; the mil-sim doctrine lean (BL-277 q5) reads creed weights that now have generated content behind them.
5. **Scope guard.** Era -1 sandbox first; whether 1960-era Io surfaces any of this is a separate, later call.

items.title: Re-site the GOE gate to its own epoch with a re-derived, epoch-relative threshold
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-04 off NR-046: S6 now tests the NOE against tectonic vigour at the NOE's own epoch, but the GOE gate deliberately still reads present-day theta — its 2.4 upper bound was calibrated against present-day values, and naively re-siting it dropped acceptance 78.5% -> 60.2% (69% of new rejects Mat Worlds), so that half was reverted. This item closes the asymmetry properly: express the GOE bound epoch-relatively (e.g. as a multiple of the reference world's theta AT the GOE epoch), re-derive the constant, and verify with the C1 rejection census that acceptance and lean costs hold.
items.design:
## Intent (design-owed)

The physically coherent end state is both S6 oxygen gates reading tectonic state at their own epoch. The NOE half landed 2026-08-04 (theta_at/mobile_lid_at in planetology.cpp); the GOE half is a calibration project, not a one-line change — the measured 60.2% run is the evidence.

Method sketch:
1. Compute the reference (Sol-default) world's theta at its GOE epoch; express the current 2.4 absolute bound as a ratio against it.
2. Re-site the gate to test theta_at(age - goe_at) against that ratio-derived bound.
3. Regression: C1 rejection census in planetology_sweep — acceptance within ~1% of baseline, no lean above ~2 draws, Mat World share stable.
4. Update PLANETOLOGY.md and remove the asymmetry comment at the S6 site.

Until this lands, the documented asymmetry (NOE historical / GOE present-day) is a known position, not a bug — present-day theta is conservative for an upper bound because heat only falls.

items.title: A fresh CMake configure cannot download SDL3 on this machine (TLS revocation failure)
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-04 off NR-048, upgraded from observation after the recommended retry REPRODUCED it (curl to codeload.github.com fails TLS, exit 35; CMake reports "unable to check revocation for the certificate" in FetchContent_MakeAvailable(SDL3), CMakeLists.txt:44). Existing build dirs are unaffected (populated _deps), which hides it — but a fresh clone, a new git worktree, or a CI runner cannot configure at all, and it blocked BL-287's from-cold timing measurement. Candidate fixes: vendor the dep, point FetchContent at a local cache/mirror (FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_SDL3), or settle the machine's schannel revocation posture. items.title: Visualise the political steps of generation — watch nations carve territory and corporations seed assets
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-04 to complete the "each step" coverage of Ben's v0.1.6 generation-visibility steer. The physical steps have visibility designed (BL-256 globe for the forming world, BL-303/304 for the tile passes, BL-211 for the narrative); the POLITICAL steps have none — the Voronoi BFS territory carve, nation resource-profile derivation, and corporation asset seeding all happen invisibly between one generation-screen stage and the next. Design owed: what a watchable nation/corp generation pass looks like (staged claims on the globe/canvas? a replay scrubber? per-nation derivation cards?), and where it lives (generation screen vs post-hoc ledger).
items.design:
## Intent (design-owed)

Questions the design must settle:
1. **Live or replay?** Show the carve as it generates (generation-screen stage, BL-256's globe as the surface) or as a post-hoc scrubbable replay (Generation Ledger sibling)? The BFS is deterministic and fast, so both are cheap; the difference is where the player is standing.
2. **What of the corp step is visible?** Asset placement is spatial (canvas-friendly); financial-profile derivation is not (card-friendly). Probably both, split by surface.
3. **Coverage check** — after this, walk GENERATION_STRATEGY.md's pass map and confirm every step has a named visibility surface; any without one gets an explicit "invisible by design" note there.

## SETTLED 2026-08-08 (Ben)

- **The territory carve is watched live**, as a generation-screen stage extending BL-256's globe — not deferred to a post-hoc replay. It joins the staged New World wizard steps the player already watches rather than living only in the Ledger.
- **The corp-seeding step gets both surfaces, split by kind**: asset placement renders spatially on the canvas/globe (it's positional, so the canvas is where it belongs); financial-profile derivation surfaces as a card/ledger entry (it isn't positional, so a canvas overlay would be the wrong shape for it).
- The coverage-check task (walk GENERATION_STRATEGY.md's pass map, note any step still invisible-by-design) stays in scope as the item's closing step, unchanged.

items.title: Record campaign firsts (deeds) as world-history-log entries — no gating, just the story beats
items.summary: The Era 1 tree draft's deed primitive (docs/research/ERA1_TECH_LANDSCAPE.md § The deed primitive) is design-owed and gates real keystones — too early to build. But recording campaign firsts (first off-world launch, first building on a second body) as plain world_history_entry lines, gating nothing, is buildable now on the landed BL-208 log and makes deeds observable for match reports and, later, the strategy library's ⚠-marked deed facts (STRATEGIES.md § The design-gap yield).
items.design:
## Design pass done 2026-08-09 — and it resolves the open call AGAINST the item's own lean

The item asked: reuse an existing `history_topic` (`decision` or `agency`) **tagged** as a first, or
add a new topic value? It leaned toward reusing with a tag, on the reasoning that the Era 1 tree's
deed primitive — subject/scope/count/recorded — is a richer object this item should not pre-empt.

**Add a `deed` topic value.** Three reasons, and the first is decisive.

### 1. "Tagged" means widening the struct, which was rejected days ago for exactly this

`world_history_entry` (world.hpp) is `{timestamp, topic, body, corp, event, consequence}`. There is
no spare field to mean "this one is a first" — tagging requires ADDING one. And **BL-282 settled
that trade-off on 2026-08-03** (Ben, NR-030 option 2), refusing a `body_b` field with the reasoning
that it *"would change a struct four other call sites depend on, for one topic's need, and would
leave every other topic carrying a field it never sets."*

A `first` flag is the same shape of change for the same class of reason. The precedent is days old
and points the other way from this item's lean. A new enum value costs one line and no reader
changes — every existing consumer switches on `topic` and simply never matches it.

### 2. `trade_route` already IS a "first" topic

The enum's own comment: *"A trade_route's FIRST establishment (not repeat traffic on an existing
lane)."* So a topic meaning "a campaign first" is not a new concept being invented here — it is the
concept the log already uses, and `deed` generalises it rather than contradicting it.

### 3. A topic is not the primitive, so nothing is pre-empted

The item's worry was shipping "a half-shaped enum value" ahead of the deed primitive. But the topic
answers a different question from the primitive. The TOPIC says *this log line records a campaign
first*; the PRIMITIVE (subject/scope/count/recorded) is a richer object that would live elsewhere
and could later EMIT entries under this topic. Adding the topic constrains the primitive's shape not
at all — whereas a `first` flag on every entry would be the half-shaped thing, since it asserts the
distinction is a property of every log line rather than of a kind of line.

## What to build

- `history_topic::deed`, documented in the enum the way its siblings are.
- Candidate firsts, both readable from existing `supply_system.cpp` dispatch code as the item says:
  **first launch-dispatch to space**, and **first building on a second body**.
- **World-scoped**: only the FIRST corporation to do it fires the line, per the STRATEGIES.md
  ST-10 / NR-069 lean toward world-scoped deeds. That needs a one-per-world latch; put it on
  `world` beside the log, not in UI state — a deed that re-fires on reload is not a first.
- Timestamp is the sim day tick, matching `decision`/`agency`/`trade_route` (the topic-scoped clock
  rule in AI_OPPONENT.md § 8a).
- **No gating.** The item's title is explicit: this records story beats, it does not unlock anything.

## Verification

`history_log_harness`: each deed fires exactly once across a run where two corporations both
qualify; the entry carries the right body/corp tags; a second qualifying event adds no entry.
Determinism: same seed, same deeds, same order.

ANCIENT_TECH_LADDER.md § Geometry (settled 2026-08-04, Ben) already specifies the intended shape in full: a Path-of-Exile-style radial web — rings are bands/eras (time, centre-out), sectors are domains (angle), keystone forks carry visible exclusion, travel is OR/meaning is AND. This item is the implementation of that already-settled design for the two authored eras, not new design. Also flips nav rail slot 4 (Research, previously hard-disabled) to open the same viewer, per Ben's request 2026-08-06.

items.title: Works Doctrine as a corporation-generation input — State Arsenal nations may not charter a specialist corporation at all

items.title: Unit verb family for the action dictionary — levy/march/garrison/scout at unit grain, design-owed until a unit_command seam exists to transcribe from
items.summary: The verb half of the unit dictionary — the military gameplay.* family ACTIONS.json entirely lacks (all 11 gameplay entries are economic). SANDBOX-0CE.md already names the four verbs by their building analogues: levy/raise (≈ build), march (≈ place_road’s route binds), garrison/disband (≈ idle/demolish), scout (≈ survey). Filed design-owed rather than authored: there is no unit_command seam to transcribe from, and authoring dictionary entries ahead of code inverts BL-270’s transcription discipline — the exact failure mode that makes a dictionary lie about a seam.
items.design:
## Session rulings (2026-08-07, Ben)

- **Roster now, verbs design-owed** — the ruled split. UNITS.json (the noun half, BL-274) ships first; this item holds the verb half open with the transcription debt NAMED: entries are written only when a unit_command seam exists, then transcribed from it, preconditions mirroring its rejection enum exactly as the gameplay family mirrors corp_command_result.
- **Verbs act at UNIT grain** (BL-157 amendment carries the same ruling). Args bind a unit id; no force record, no province-grain manpower verbs — raise_manpower stays a sim-internal call, not a dictionary press.
- **Verbs are era-invariant.** Era-keying lives in UNITS.json’s availability derivation; one precondition string per raising verb points at it ("the unit type is in the acting nation’s available roster — see UNITS.json").
- **Military ideology bias is DOCTRINE PREFERENCE, not per-verb keys** — VOICES.json’s doctrine_preference field (authored 2026-08-07): per-stance multipliers over siege_stance plus a frontal_risk scalar. The scorer applies it where a doctrine_row is chosen (BL-277’s seam), so a war-leaning creed changes HOW it fights before any verb exists.
- Diplomacy verbs at nation grain (offer_peace, demand_tribute, propose_pact, threaten) stay BL-297’s, not this item’s.

## Deliverable when unblocked

The gameplay.* military entries in ACTIONS.json (canonical), rendered mirrors, PHRASINGS.json stance sets per verb (Battery B’s reserved slots), and the SANDBOX-0CE Battery B run that tests era-portability of the stance taxonomy.

items.title: The armed trading house's conflict spine - units as tokens on the tile map, and a campaign battle resolver with seeded randomness and withdrawal
items.summary: REPHRASED 2026-08-10 (BL-094's rewrite, NR-120): the actor this item is written for is now the national private militia, not a governing body. What the item OWNS is unchanged — the campaign-era military design the prototype has none of, engine-parity with BL-272/Era −1's resolve_battle — but its reach is narrower and sharper: not "how law, policy and force reach military outcomes" but how the militia's PROCUREMENT (what it can field, bought from independent suppliers) and its ANSWERABILITY (law/policy it operates inside, not instruments it wields) both cash out in the 1960+ campaign. Promoted by the rewrite from a BL-094 follow-on to the item Sprint 8 designs directly — the conflict spine is the militia's whole reason to exist, not a subsystem it acquires later.
items.design:
## Filed at the 2026-08-07 military design session

- **Bounding rule (Sprint-2 precedent, carried on Ben’s ruling): specify against nation identity, never against derivation.** The v0.1.x stubs (BL-155 laws, BL-156 techs, BL-157 units, BL-158 sentiment) design against this item’s target without waiting for BL-094’s full landing.
- Scope at filing, deliberately thin until promotion: (1) the force-command model — who orders units in the 1960 era and through which seam (the future unit_command, BL-314’s transcription target, should be THIS design’s seam, not a sandbox-only one); (2) the law→military reach — which BL-155 law classes produce military consequences (conscription, embargo enforcement, basing rights); (3) engine parity — the 1960 roster as the last UNITS.json rows, no second combat path.
- Movement, stacking, supply-to-units and unit production stay out of the v0.1.x stubs and inside this item’s eventual promotion — the "Conflict proper" boundary BL-157 and BL-189’s closure both point at.
- Design here is a PROMOTION COST of BL-094: do not promote this item ahead of BL-094’s own landing sequence (the parked-cascade warning in BL-094 stands).

## 2026-08-10 — rephrased for the militia (Sprint 8, BL-094's rewrite)

This item's scope is unchanged by the rewrite — force-command model, law→military reach,
engine parity with the 1960 roster — but two of its three named strands need a militia reading,
not a governing-body one:

1. **Force-command model.** Unchanged in shape: who orders units, through which seam
   (the future `unit_command`, BL-314's transcription target). The militia commands directly —
   this was already how a "governing body" would have worked at the unit-command grain, so
   nothing here actually moves.
2. **Law→military reach — REPHRASED.** Was: "which BL-155 law classes produce military
   consequences (conscription, embargo enforcement, basing rights)", framed as laws the player
   PASSES. Now: which BL-155 law classes the militia is **subject to** and must operate under —
   an embargo it must route procurement around, basing rights it must be granted rather than
   grant, conscription as something that could apply *to* its recruitment pool rather than
   something it enacts. Same law classes, opposite direction of agency.
3. **Engine parity.** Unchanged: the 1960 roster is the last `UNITS.json` rows, no second
   combat path.

**New strand this item should carry once promoted, not yet designed here:** the procurement→field
pipeline is the militia's *actual* route to fielding a force (BL-350 owns the contract mechanic;
this item owns what happens once the contracted materiel arrives — unit production/assembly from
delivered equipment rather than from a corporation's own factories). Filed as a dependency note,
not expanded — BL-350 lands first.

Bounding rule from the 2026-08-07 filing still holds: specify against nation identity (now:
militia identity), never against derivation. Do not promote ahead of BL-094's own landing.

## SETTLED 2026-08-13 (Ben, elicitation Q&A) - the ancient reading

The item was written for a 1960 national private militia and required BL-094, which is
parked with the space arc. Ben's four rulings re-point it at the ancient campaign and
**overturn one strand it has carried since filing**.

### 1. The player is an ARMED TRADING HOUSE, and its label is a consequence of policy

Not a militia, and deliberately **not fixed as "mercenary"** - Ben: *"we need to ensure
that mercenary isn't too strict a term. Depending on policy, it could be army or pirate
as well."* The same company, the same units, the same verbs; what changes is who is
paying and what the surrounding polities call it. Trade is the base identity and force is
what protects and extends it - so the conflict spine hangs off the commercial spine
rather than replacing it.

Design consequence: there is no `mercenary` class anywhere in the model. There is a
company with force, a contract seam (BL-377) supplying the *reason*, and policy/standing
supplying the *name*. Army, mercenary and pirate are three readings of one object, and
the reading is derived, never authored.

### 2. Command grain: UNITS AS TOKENS ON THE TILE MAP, fighting directly

Not armies at province grain, and not contracts-only. The player moves units on the tile
map and they fight where they stand. This is the grain BL-314's `unit_command`
transcription target must be written against, and it is a heavier commitment than the
province-grain sim the Era -1 machinery uses - see section 3.

### 3. TWO COMBAT PATHS - this REVERSES the item's engine-parity strand

The item said, from its 2026-08-07 filing through its 2026-08-10 rephrase: *"engine
parity - the 1960 roster as the last UNITS.json rows, no second combat path."* Ben has
ruled the opposite: **campaign battles get their own resolver.**

Why the reversal is right rather than merely different: the Era -1 sim resolves a battle
between two PROVINCES in a year tick, as one scored outcome. The campaign resolves a
fight between TOKENS ON TILES, with position, withdrawal, and a player watching. Those
are not the same question, and one function answering both would either flatten the
campaign fight into a dice roll or drag tile-grain state into a generation pass with no
room for it. The shared thing is the roster and the calibration constants, not the
resolver.

**The cost is now explicit and must be paid deliberately**: two paths can drift. The
mitigation is that the ROSTER stays single-sourced - one unit table, one set of power
numbers - and any divergence in outcome between the two resolvers is a finding to
explain, not a fact to accept.

### 4. Battle resolution: uncertain to the player, deterministic to the engine

Ben: *"Resolution of battles should have an element of randomness, and the option to
withdraw after a short time."*

Randomness and the determinism invariant are **not in conflict here**, and the
distinction is load-bearing: the resolver draws from a SEEDED stream folded from the
battle's own identity, so the same save replayed produces the same battle - while the
player, who cannot see the seed, faces a genuinely uncertain fight. Do not reach for
wall-clock or unseeded RNG; that breaks replay for a feeling seeded draws already give.

**Withdrawal is a first-class verb, not a failure state.** "After a short time" means a
fight is not resolved in one instant: it runs long enough for the player to read how it
is going and pull out, paying a cost. That makes committing force a decision under
uncertainty rather than a coin-flip, and it is what stops randomness reading as unfair.

### 5. The ground it stands on: worked tiles and a structure of civilisation

Ben: *"We need to make sure that tiles are suitably worked and there's a structure of
civilisation."* The conflict spine is worth nothing on an empty map - a contract to take
a place only means something if the place is worked, populated and owned. This is a
PRECONDITION on the item, and it points at the Era -1 works roster (BL-321) and the
generated background industry as its suppliers. Before promoting this item, walk the
homeworld at 0 CE and confirm there is a civilisation there to fight over.

### 6. The law strand is SPLIT OUT

The third strand - which law classes the company is subject to and must operate under -
leaves this item and becomes **BL-380 (the company's answerability)**. It was always a
different question from how force reaches an outcome, and at 0 CE, with no law system
live, it would have blocked a buildable item behind an unbuilt one.

### What this item now owns

The force-command model at unit-token grain, the campaign battle resolver (seeded
randomness plus withdrawal), and the single-sourced roster shared with the Era -1 sim.
It no longer owns law reach, and it no longer requires BL-094.

items.title: Era -1 logistics: real terrain in battles, terrain-weighted reach, and a supply burden that grows with the empire
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-04 from Ben's question: 'how is logistics factored into our generation? It should definitely be tangibly harder to supply more provinces, and fight further away battles.' Investigation found it essentially is not. Three real logistics systems exist (logistics.cpp's terrain-weighted A* with road discounts, supply_system, road_generation) and the Era -1 sim uses NONE of them; its supply is one line of straight-line Chebyshev distance. Worse, the sim passes a NULL terrain view, so every battle in every run is fought on default grassland/plains and the whole terrain_combat module (including BL-233's modifiers) is inert. And there is no per-holding cost of any kind: holding 500 provinces costs exactly what holding 5 costs.
items.design:
## What the investigation found

**1. Supply's entire dynamic range is 10% of combat power.** In combat.cpp supply only mitigates ATTRITION, and attrition is `terrain_attrition x season`. With a null terrain view every battle resolves on grassland/plains, where attrition is 100/1000. So fully supplied costs 0% and TOTALLY CUT OFF costs 10%. That is noise against roster modifiers, and it is why a province 34 tiles away was taken at 5% supply in the vacuous-stall test (pre-rebase id BL-312, since reassigned; landed 2026-08-05, 'Four review items').

**2. The terrain module is inert.** Both callers (the sweep and the Ages view) pass `sim_terrain_view{}`. A mountain battle would carry up to 900/1000 attrition and supply would matter enormously - but no Era -1 battle has ever been fought on real ground.

**3. There is no cost of breadth at all.** Not weak - absent. No upkeep, no administrative drag, no garrison burden, no distance-from-capital penalty on holdings.

## Three slices

**S1 - real terrain.** Build the terrain view from the body's tiles and pass it. Nearly free, makes terrain_combat live, and sharpens everything the sweep measures.

**S2 - terrain-weighted reach.** Replace Chebyshev distance-from-capital with a cost computed over the neighbour graph using the landform traversal costs logistics.cpp already defines (plains 1.0 -> mountain 2.0). Computed by Dijkstra from the capital and cached until the capital changes, so the per-year cost stays a lookup.

**S3 - the burden of breadth.** Supply available to any campaign falls with the polity's total holdings. This is the mechanism Ben asked for and the one BL-277's (Era -1 military strategy) answered Q2 wrongly claimed already existed - an answer that now survives only in the 2026-08-05 commits, since the 2026-08-07 rebase dropped it from the item's design prose. With it, the frontier stall becomes arithmetic rather than a `w_dist` scoring preference.

## Why this is priority A

It is the missing physical constraint under three open findings. The no-elimination finding (nobody is ever eliminated; pre-rebase id BL-308, reassigned by the 2026-08-07 rebase; retired as a standalone item by Ben's same-day ruling - the target, elimination possible and subject-nation release possible, is recorded on BL-271) and BL-277's (Era -1 military strategy) corrected Q2 (the stall is a preference, not a limit; the correction lives in the 2026-08-05 review commit) both trace back to expansion being free. Empires grow without limit because nothing charges them for size.

items.title: Pre-history timelapse in the New World wizard - the generated world's two thousand years replay on the generating screen before the campaign starts
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-07 from Ben's aim: the New World wizard should render a timelapse of the world's simulated past - 'a massive change, requiring AI to play, and an entire sandbox pre-history, which should be a documented aim by now.' The substrate largely exists and this item CONSUMES it, never duplicates it: BL-271's Era -1 sim (deterministic year-tick 0-1960) whose owner_changes list was built as the time-lapse substrate, and the landed Ages view ('The Ages view: two thousand years of borders, scrubbable', 2026-08-04) that already replays it - deliberately outside the generation path, leaving BL-271 open question 2 unanswered. This item answers Q2 yes and Q3 yes-for-watching: the sim runs at generation time with the world seed, and the generating screen gains a playback surface upgraded from province dots to filled territory. The 'AI playing' is BL-271's deterministic polity scorer - never a live model, never a cloud call.
items.design:
## The aim (Ben, 2026-08-07)

The New World wizard eventually renders a timelapse of pre-history: the generated world's simulated past playing out visually before the campaign starts. This item is that documented aim. The sandbox exists (BL-271); the AI that plays it is that sim's deterministic scored-utility polity layer.

**Supersession note (dated 2026-08-07, newest wins):** BL-271's summary bounds the sim to 'behind a harness flag / tools target, never in the shipped campaign path'. This item supersedes that bound for the GENERATION path only: one seeded run during world generation. The harness/tools uses stay.

## What already exists - consume, don't rebuild

- **The sim.** BL-271's year-tick loop 0-1960 (src/world/history_sim.{hpp,cpp}): deterministic, seeded, integer-only; polities settle, campaign, invest; battles resolve through combat.cpp. A shared-currency scorer redesign is in the staged working tree as of filing (no id - re-file if it stalls).
- **The replay substrate.** owner_changes + owner_slice_at - delta-encoded ownership history, any year in one forward walk. Built for exactly this (Ben, 2026-08-04, history_sim.hpp).
- **The playback surface.** The Ages view (src/ui/tile_inspector.cpp): Play/Pause/Restart, year slider, polity-coloured province dots. Landed 2026-08-04 (requirements group history-ages-view).
- **Determinism proof.** BL-275's sweep asserts re-run reproduction and per-seed divergence; BL-298's battery (designed) adds replay conformance over the diplomacy seam.

## What this item builds

**S1 - settle BL-271 Q2: the sim runs at generation time.** One seeded run during the staged generation screen, keyed off the WORLD seed (not the Ages view's hard-coded seed 7), with real creed_state and the real terrain view (BL-316 S1 / sim_terrain_build.hpp). Outputs feed the BL-208 history log.

**S2 - the wizard playback surface.** The generating screen gains the timelapse: the run completes, then plays back via owner_slice_at with captions from the sim's dated history_event lines. Skippable - but the sim ALWAYS runs to completion identically whether the player watches or skips; playback is replay of a finished run, so player input timing can never touch generated state (determinism guard).

**S3 - filled territory.** Upgrade the render from province-anchor dots to filled territory / borders, shared with the Ages view via one extracted playback component.

**S4 - Ages view coherence.** The Ages view must consume the STORED generation-time run (same seed, same terrain, same creeds), not lazily re-run with its own seed - otherwise the ledger shows a different history than the one that shaped generation.

## Hard constraints

- **Replay, never live play.** The timelapse renders a completed, seeded, deterministic run. No live agent in the generation path. Richer AI (AI_OPPONENT.md sec 10, Project-Rival findings) tunes the scorer OFFLINE; it never sits in the wizard.
- **No cloud.** No HTTP client, no API key, no cloud dependency.
- **No duplication.** BL-271 owns the sim; the Ages view stays as the post-hoc surface (upgraded, S4); this item is the generation-time consumer.
- **Names.** Everything shown is seeded sci-fi/fantasy naming; Rome stays a mechanism reference.

## Scope fences against siblings

- **BL-305 (generation political visibility):** constrained to the post-sim 1960 carve/seeding; its floated 'replay scrubber' idea lives HERE, not there.
- **BL-256 (generation globe):** its not-in-scope list ('any post-generation overlay', 'cities, borders') is amended by S2/S3 only when this item lands; until then the globe stays pure.

## Watchability prerequisites

The payoff needs a sim worth watching. The settle-occupancy fix moved the last ownership change from year 458 to 967 of 1960; the staged scorer redesign aims further. Before S2 ships, re-measure: a timelapse where the last three-quarters is inert is not a first-impression payoff. Runtime budget: the full run measured ~2.1s after province growth was fixed (correct behaviour, more work) - budget it inside the generating screen's existing wait, not the wizard's interactive rounds.

## Version note

post-v0.1.0, contingent on BL-271 and BL-316 (both post-v0.1.0). The wizard preview pane (built 2026-08-07, unnumbered session work) is the natural S2 surface and already ships the async-build pattern S1 needs.

## The route (2026-08-07 ultracode plan, judged 3-draft panel)

Six stages from Project-Rival's current state to the watched timelapse; full trace in-session, NR-078.

**Determinate-but-text-based, in one paragraph:** pre-history is determinate because the only author is the deterministic sim (integer, RNG-free; owner_changes is the substrate, byte-identity harness-asserted). It becomes text-based at three layers: AUTHORED - models work only offline, distilling Rival play into committed schema-versioned data (VOICES/UNITS/PHRASINGS.json), numbers and doctrine only, never names; EMITTED - the sim records its typed decisions ({year, polity, verb, target, winter, score}) as a trace from which owner_changes is fully derivable, so the transcript IS the history; RENDERED - a pure seeded chronicle renderer expands trace records through committed template banks into dated two-column lines (settlement.cpp idiom), bridged into the BL-208 history log. {world seed + artifact schema versions} is the complete replay key.

**S1 - land the substrate, fix the instrument.** Scoped-commit the staged scorer arc under a minted id; fix two CONFIRMED sweep defects (168x90 vs Kepler's 180x84 at history_sweep.cpp:192/195/380 - silent terrain misalignment since 168*90==180*84; the S2 recheck runs no_terrain against real-terrain rows); fix sim_terrain_build.hpp's 'BL-314 S1' label (means BL-316 S1); reconcile the three runtime claims (<1s / ~600ms / ~2.1s); re-measure last-change-year as the watchability baseline; correct BL-271/BL-275 statuses.

**S2 - the decision trace (NEW item: era1-decision-trace).** Persist the already-computed sim_verb decisions + battle records; wire creed_state through both callers so polities carry seeded names; fix the 'Reach Reach' daughter naming; harness-assert (a) byte-identical trace per seed and (b) owner_changes fully derivable from the trace - transcript = history.

**S3 - the chronicle renderer (NEW item: chronicle-renderer).** The one unbuilt piece no item names: pure seeded renderer, ONE neutral chronicler register v1 (voice packs deferred), schema-versioned template banks recorded in the run header, no-Earth-noun grep check, bridge into world::history_log.

**S4 - one history per world (this item's S1+S4, pulled early).** Generation-time run on the world seed with real creeds + real terrain, stored in the save; Ages view re-based onto the stored run, its seed-7u private re-run deleted.

**S5 - the watched timelapse (this item's S2; S3 filled-territory deferred).** Playback on the generating screen: dots + chronicle captions, skippable; skip-vs-watch identical world hash, harness-asserted; visual-verify capture; gated on the S1 watchability re-measure.

**S6 - the calibration loop (BL-297 gated by BL-298).** BL-298 checks 1-2 built and green BEFORE any model connects; nation verbs on the existing MCP server; sim verb family transcribed into ACTIONS.json (transcription, not invention); first Rival campaign year; weights land only as versioned artifact diffs. Changes who plays, not what is watched - sequenced after S5, and the recovery path if watchability stays shallow.

**Load-bearing risks:** the sweep grid bug contaminates any calibration citing pre-fix evidence; watchability is the unknown that gates S5; the arc is post-v0.1.0 - ROADMAP.md owns sequence, resequencing is Ben's call; BL-279's trace schema is corp-grain with no nation-grain variant (must be decided at BL-297 landing or Rival logs won't double as corpus).

## 2026-08-10 — re-versioned by the Sprints 8-12 plan (v0.3.0 -> v0.1.7)

Moved v0.3.0 -> v0.1.7. This is a generation-VISIBILITY surface that consumes BL-271 (complete), not an Era -1 sim item — it was only in v0.3.0 because NR-101 swept it there with the rest of the Era -1 prose. Ben named it at Sprint 5's close as the piece still owed. Cut by Sprint 12. Option on the table, not taken: ride it with BL-264 in Sprint 11, since both are New World wizard stages, which would land it three sprints earlier for little extra.

The shared-currency scorer redesign - settle/campaign/invest/consolidate priced in one commensurable currency so the incommensurable-verb stall (last ownership change year 458 of 1960 at first cut, 967 after the settle-occupancy fix) stops being a scoring artifact - plus the BL-316 S1 terrain adapter (sim_terrain_build.hpp) wiring real Kepler ground into Era -1 battles. Landing commit also fixes two sweep-instrument defects found by the 2026-08-07 plan review: the sweep passed 168x90 where Kepler is 180x84 (equal tile counts, so every terrain lookup misaligned SILENTLY), and the S2 determinism recheck ran an empty terrain view against real-terrain rows (a guaranteed false FAIL once terrain changes any decision). No calibration may cite pre-fix sweep evidence. PARKED RED (Ben, 2026-08-07: generation parks): the landing commit carries five failing campaign assertions (R3a/R3a2/R3a3/R3b/R5 - campaigning behaviour under the mid-flight shared-currency scorer) named in its message; completion is owed when the scorer goes green.
