items.title: Era -1 sim runtime: R7 (full 0-1960 run under a second) fails at ~2.1s for the right reason
items.summary: RECOVERED 2026-08-07: this item was filed 2026-08-04 in the pre-rebase tree and lost when the history rewrite dropped the local commits' backlog edits (NR-079's class); text restored verbatim from the stash. Requirement R7 (a full 0-1960 run completes under a second) now FAILS at ~2.1s. The cause is correct behaviour, not a regression in the bad sense: the settle-occupancy fix stopped the Settle verb stacking provinces on one cell, so Kepler now reaches ~749 real provinces instead of ~191, and the sim does roughly four times the work. The per-year neighbour scan and the O(provinces) occupancy search are the two obvious costs. Until fixed, the harness R7 bound is relaxed to the measured reality (BL-318's landing commit) rather than left red.
items.design:
## Why it is slow now

Two loops scale with the province count: the occupancy search in Settle scans every province for a free cell, and the per-polity holdings scan runs each year. Both were cheap when the map collapsed into 33 cells.

## Fix direction

A spatial index (cell -> province) removes the occupancy scan outright. Holdings could be maintained incrementally rather than rebuilt each tick.

## Do not fix by capping provinces

The province growth is the thing that made history run twice as long. Trading it back for runtime would undo the improvement.

## Why it matters more now (2026-08-07)

BL-317 S4 runs this sim inside world generation; the runtime budget there is the generating screen's wait. The ~2.1s figure is the number S4 must budget against until this item lands.

items.title: Era -1 works: the pre-history building list - an authored, endowment-gated table of what a polity builds, and what those works do to reach, capacity and defence
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-07 from Ben's question: 'do we have a list of buildings for the pre-history generation?' Investigation: no, and no place one would go. The Era -1 layer has NO building noun whatsoever - province (settlement.hpp:74) holds endowment windows, an industrial clock, population and manpower, but nothing built. Units got their noun axis (unit_roster.{hpp,cpp}, BL-274); works are the missing half. The gap is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: BL-316 charges a polity for breadth but gives it NOTHING TO BUY to extend reach, so the only strategy against the burden of breadth is to stop expanding. Works are the counter-move that makes the frontier stall a decision instead of a ceiling.
items.design:
## The shape - mirror unit_roster, do NOT reuse building_component

This is BL-274's sibling on the noun axis, and it copies that item's settled shape verbatim: an **authored C++ table**, four bands (reuse `roster_band`), rows gated on the province endowment windows the settlement pass already computes, availability **derived from the ground** - no research, no unlock events, no player choice.

**It must not reuse `building_component`** (components.hpp:252). That struct is the campaign-era building: a tile entity carrying a recipe index, a workforce target, an auto-solver flag, credit/resource build cost, per-tick maintenance and wages, decommission state and construction ticks. Era -1 has no credits, no market, no recipe registry and no economy tick - it has a year loop over provinces. Sharing the struct would drag the whole campaign economy into the generation layer to satisfy fields nothing sets. A work is instead a small id held by the *province*, not an entity on a tile.

## Storage: C++ table, not Lua (decision taken 2026-08-07, see NR)

The campaign era authors building data in Lua (`scripts/economy.lua` -> `building_economics`, `scripts/recipes.lua` -> the recipe registry), and TECH_FOUNDATIONS names 'building definitions' as a sanctioned scripting-boundary. That precedent does **not** carry here. `recipe_registry.cpp` is the *one* TU in the project that pulls sol2/Lua; every other `src/world/*.cpp` is deliberately SDL/Lua-free so the headless harnesses build with nothing but a C++20 compiler (TECH_FOUNDATIONS.md:142-145). The Era -1 sim is verified exclusively by those harnesses (`history_sweep.cpp`, `history_sim_harness.cpp`). Putting the works table in Lua would either drag Lua into the headless world layer or force a second loading path for the same data.

So: **authored C++ table in `works_roster.cpp`**, exactly as `unit_roster.cpp` does. Lua keeps the campaign-era balance data it already owns. If the works table ever needs live retuning, the right move is to promote it *with* the unit roster, once, not to split the two.

## Rows

`work_row { const char* name; roster_band band; work_gate gate; work_effect effect; int weight; }`

`work_gate` reuses the `roster_gate` axes (ore_q / farm_q / port_q / energy_q, 0-1000 thresholds, zero = no gate) plus a population floor - a granary needs people before it needs grain.

`work_effect` deltas ONLY quantities the sim already has, per-mille:

- `capacity_mod` - the province's demographic carrying capacity (BL-273's logistic ceiling).
- `manpower_mod` - the manpower ceiling, i.e. what the province can raise.
- `reach_mod` - a discount on the terrain-weighted supply cost through/from this province. **This is the row that matters**: it is how a polity buys its way past BL-316 S3's burden of breadth.
- `defence_mod` - a modifier the province contributes to `army_stack_entry` when defending, resolved through combat.cpp's existing terrain path. Never a new combat concept.
- `industrial_mod` - pull-forward on the Stage 4 furnace date.

First-cut roster, generic mechanism nouns only (standing naming rule - no Earth proper noun, and none of these may read as recognisably Latin):

| Band | Rows |
|---|---|
| Classical | Granary, Channel Works, Ore Pits, Wall Circuit, Way Station, Harbour Mole |
| Medieval | Water Mill, Stone Fortress, Guild Quarter, Deepwater Wharf, Span Bridge |
| Gunpowder | Bastion Fort, Powder Mill, Counting House, Cut Canal, Naval Yard |
| Industrial | Blast Works, Rail Head, Signal Line, Arsenal, Coaling Station |

Bands are cumulative for the same reason the roster's are: nothing un-invents a granary.

## Who builds, and when

The sim's existing per-year polity scorer (BL-318's shared-currency verbs) gains a `build_work` verb priced in the same currency as its campaign verbs, so building a Way Station competes directly with raising an army - which is the whole point. A work is chosen by score over the available rows, paid in the shared currency, and recorded as a dated `history_event` line so it lands in the chronicle.

## What it hands the campaign (the BL-272 parity contract)

Industrial-band works are the **ancestors of `building_type`**. A province that lit Blast Works in 1780 is where the 1960 smelter sits and why its substrate density is high. Landing this closes a real gap in `substrate_density`, which is currently generated rather than earned. Scope fence: this item **records** the correspondence; consuming it in campaign generation is a follow-on, not a slice here.

## Slices

- **S1** - `works_roster.{hpp,cpp}`: the table, the gate check, `available_works(province, band)`. Pure, headless-testable, no sim changes. Mirrors unit_roster's own first cut.
- **S2** - province storage: a small `std::vector<uint8_t>` (or bitmask) of built work ids on `province`, plus the effect accumulators the sim reads.
- **S3** - the `build_work` verb in the scorer, priced in the shared currency; dated history lines.
- **S4** - wire `reach_mod` into BL-316's terrain-weighted reach and `defence_mod` into the combat path; re-run the sweep and report whether the frontier stall moved from ceiling to decision.

## Sequencing

**Requires BL-316 (Era -1 logistics) to land first.** S4 has nothing to discount until terrain-weighted reach exists, and the item's whole justification is the counter-move to BL-316 S3. Filed priority A for that coupling, not for urgency against v0.1.1 - ROADMAP.md owns the sequence.

## S1 landed 2026-08-07 (same session as filing)

src/world/works_roster.{hpp,cpp} + tools/verify/works_roster_harness.cpp — the table (21 rows across the four bands), the gate check, available_works, work_id and total_work_effect. 22 assertions PASS over R1-R7. Pure and standalone: no sim change, no province-struct change, nothing wired. CMake needs no edit (both source lists are GLOB CONFIGURE_DEPENDS).

R7 is the assertion worth keeping: every reach-bearing work must be gateable by some ground, AND an endowment-poor province must still be able to raise one. Without that second half, poor ground has no way to buy reach and BL-316 S3 stays a ceiling rather than a decision — the exact failure this item exists to prevent.

S2-S4 remain, and S4 is still gated on BL-316 (era -1 logistics): reach_mod has nothing to discount until terrain-weighted reach exists.

## S2-S4 landed 2026-08-13

**S2 — province storage.** `province::works_built` is a 32-bit MASK plus five plain-int
accumulators (`work_capacity_mod` .. `work_industrial_mod`), not the vector the design
offered: the struct is copied on every Settle and lives in a vector that grows past 400 entries
inside a pass already costing ~23 s of a ~25 s world, so heap ownership per province was the
wrong trade. Plain ints rather than a `work_effect` member because works_roster.hpp
forward-declares `province` — including it back would close a cycle to store five numbers.
The mask imposes a 32-row ceiling, now checked by the loader (a 33rd row would validate and then
be unbuildable). `apply_work_to_province` maintains the accumulators incrementally and REFUSES
a double build, which is what makes a province’s works a finite, saturating investment.

**S3 — the `build_work` verb.** A fifth scored candidate in BL-309’s shared currency, priced in
the ROUND it consumes rather than in a treasury Era -1 does not have. A work’s benefit splits by
who receives it: local effects against the province’s own endowment, reach against the polity’s
MEAN holding (against the total it was worth ~40x every local effect and the roster collapsed to
its five road rows). Bounded to two candidate provinces per polity per round — capital plus one
rotated by a hash of (polity, year, slot) — because scoring every holding is O(held x rows) in the
sim’s hot loop. Band keyed off MATERIALS capacity, not military.

**S4 — the consumers.** Every effect axis reaches something real: `capacity_mod` into a new
`province_carrying_capacity(farm_q, mod)` overload that raises the logistic ASYMPTOTE (and into
the Settle verb’s pressure test, which must divide by the same K); `manpower_mod` into
`manpower_ceiling(pop, mod)` read by `replenish_manpower`; `reach_mod` into BOTH the staging
hub’s terrain-cost discount (scorer and execution, which must agree) and the polity’s mean relief
on BL-314’s burden of breadth; `defence_mod` into defender readiness via `roster_stack`, and
into the scorer so a polity does not walk into an unseen bastion.

**One recorded divergence: `industrial_mod`.** The design calls it a pull-forward on the Stage 4
furnace date, which is not implementable — Stage 4 runs in `run_settlement`, finished before this
loop starts. Wired instead to the capacity ladder, which is what the sim actually has as an
industrial clock. NR-195 records the call.

**Wiring.** `run_history_sim` and `make_hard_coded_world` both take a defaulted
`const works_registry*`; app loads the table before generation via a new idempotent
`ensure_works_loaded()` (it previously loaded inside `load_economy`, which runs AFTER
`setup_world` — generation would have seen an empty table; NR-196).

**Verification.** `history_sweep` carries the roster on every run, reports works-raised per
world, and gates W1..W7: endowment gates fire and poor ground still gets a reach work, the
population floor gates independently, bands gate and stay cumulative, a work applies once and
refuses twice, the accumulators agree with a fresh recompute, capacity works leave a world
carrying more people, a null registry disables the verb entirely, two runs at one seed raise the
same works on the same provinces, and pre-built reach measurably changes the supply path.

**Uncalibrated.** Every magnitude in works.lua and every `w_work_*` weight is an authored
placeholder in the same sense as the surrounding `w_*` weights. Whether the frontier stall
actually moved from ceiling to decision is BL-275’s sweep to answer, not this item’s. NR-198.

items.title: next_id.js scans 0 refs - its cross-branch collision defence is silently disabled, and backlog.json is being appended to concurrently with no locking
items.summary: Found 2026-08-07 while allocating an id, and it cost a real collision. next_id.js reports 'Scanned N distinct BL-ids across 0 ref(s) + working tree' - ZERO refs, on a repo with 3 local branches and many remotes. Its refs() helper runs git for-each-ref via execSync with stderr ignored and catch-returns [] on throw; the command DOES throw inside node here while succeeding from the shell. So the tool CLAUDE.md mandates before authoring any item - the preventive half of the BL-id collision defence - silently degrades to a local-file max and defends nothing across branches. SEPARATELY and worse: backlog.json gained BL-318, BL-319 and BL-320 from another writer DURING this session, between reads minutes apart. Appending an item read-modify-write therefore duplicated BL-320; backlog_lint caught it and it was renumbered. There is no locking, no compare-and-swap, and no append helper - every writer rewrites the whole 700KB file from a snapshot.

items.title: Buildings rework - pad the roster out to the designed set, enforce placement (logistical max range above all), and make build time depend on where you build
items.summary: Commissioned by Ben 2026-08-07: 'We need to pad out the number of available buildings, and start enforcing placement rules. Especially for logistical max building range... We need to put a lot of work into this before any simulated games can occur.' Investigation confirms two of the three premises and corrects the third. CONFIRMED: the roster is thin - PRODUCTION.md designs ~26 distinct buildings against 5 generic kinds in the building_type enum and 4 recipes in the registry. CONFIRMED and worse than stated: there is NO distance or range rule in placement at all - grep for range/distance/radius across placement_rules.cpp returns nothing, so a corp may place a site arbitrarily far from any road, hub, city or port at no cost and with no refusal. CORRECTED: build time is not instant. build_duration_ticks is 2-6 econ ticks and an econ tick is a 90-day quarter, so a building takes 6 months to 18 months of game time, and BL-095 already stretches that when the market cannot supply materials (observed live 2026-08-07: 'Paused - market can't supply materials'). The real defect is that build time is a FLAT PER-TYPE CONSTANT - identical on a road-served home tile and on a mountain 40 tiles from anything.

items.title: Wire units into the campaign build - a 'hire unit' surface beside buildings, and the roster bridge it needs first
items.summary: Ben, 2026-08-07: 'Can we wire units into the main build? Perhaps we can use a hire unit button near to buildings.' The pieces exist but do not yet meet. unit_component (components.hpp:418) is a four-field stub - body, owner, count, opaque type - and unit_roster.{hpp,cpp} is a working 19-row table. Neither is reachable from the campaign: nothing constructs a unit_component, no corp_verb raises one, and no UI surface shows one. Three concrete blockers sit between here and a hire button, and the first is a design question, not a coding one.

items.title: Military bases: a muster building, hire moved onto it, and unit supply read off the shared logistics reach field
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-08 from Ben's design steer during the BL-323 reach-rule hardening: 'we need to have supply hubs for military. Perhaps we can decouple the economy and military units, so we can use military bases as tiles.' Four rulings taken live (AskUserQuestion): (1) ONE new building_type, military_base — a tile-occupying installation earning its enum value with a distinct placement rule and glyph. (2) Hiring decouples from BL-324's hire-anywhere: units muster AT a base tile, and the roster gate reads what the base's corp/body can supply — the base becomes the single economy->military interface. (3) NO second reach field: Ben's own words — 'a nation's reach for economy is also the military reach' — the existing body_reach_field IS the military supply envelope; beyond it units cannot get essential supplies (weaponry, rations). (4) Units beyond the boundary suffer deterministic per-tick strength decay — the campaign twin of the Era -1 sim's supply attrition, and the first real cost of distance for armies.
items.design:
## The four rulings (Ben, 2026-08-08, via live Q&A)

**1. One new building_type: `military_base`.** A tile-occupying installation, placed like any building (so it obeys the BL-323 reach rule and site-dependent build time for free). It earns the enum value by the settled criteria (PRODUCTION.md): a distinct placement rule and a distinct glyph. Produces nothing; staffs at zero like the port/hub.

**2. Hire moves onto the base.** BL-324's hire-anywhere is superseded: `hire_unit` requires a target tile carrying the corp's own COMPLETED military_base, and the constructed unit spawns there. The gate itself (ore/farm/port/energy axes off the corp's stockpile + port) stays as BL-324 built it for now — what changes is WHERE, not WHAT. A follow-on may localise the gate reads to the base's body; not settled here.

**3. One reach field, not two.** Ben's ruling overrode the proposed parallel base-anchored field: the ECONOMIC logistics network is the military supply envelope. `body_reach_field`'s existing anchors (cities, built ports, built hubs) define supplied ground; the military_base is NOT an anchor and extends nothing. To project force farther, extend the same network everyone else uses — roads and hubs, the exact levers BL-323 S2 priced. This is recorded as an interpretation of Ben's words ('feeds into the logistics system (directional)') in NR-091 — overturnable if misread.

**4. Out-of-supply decay.** A unit on a tile whose reach cost exceeds the authored budget (or is infinite) loses strength each economy tick — a deterministic scalar authored in economy.lua (e.g. `military.out_of_supply_decay_per_tick`), no RNG. In-range units do not regenerate under this item (healing is a later concern). This gives BL-287's future grain/fodder draws a place to land: the decay is the abstraction those consumables later replace or refine.

## Slices

**S1 — the building.** Enum value + placement rule (any owned land tile within reach; no deposit requirement) + economics entry (cost, duration, maintenance in economy.lua) + glyph (ICONS.md recipe) + Selection/hover naming. The BL-323 S3 site-time multiplier applies unchanged.

**S2 — hire-at-base.** `corp_command`'s hire_unit verb gains the base-tile precondition; the Selection element's Hire section only renders on a base tile; `corp_ai`'s hire candidate bucket scores base tiles (and a corp with no base must build one first — which the scorer prices via the existing build-candidate machinery). ACTIONS.json's hire entry updated (preconditions change — the dictionary must not go stale).

**S3 — out-of-supply decay.** In the economy tick's unit pass: units on tiles beyond the reach budget decay. Reads `tile_reach_cost` (const, cache built per-frame/tick already). Surfaces: strength shown red/depleting in the unit's Selection card.

## Sequencing

S1 -> S2 (S2 needs the building to exist) -> S3 (independent of S2 but lands the meaning). All three are small; the item is deliberately one minor's worth of work for v0.1.5 (military systems, BL-157's band).

## Not in scope

Garrison/defence mechanics, unit-vs-building interaction (undefined until BL-315's conflict spine), healing/reinforcement, grain/fodder consumables (BL-287), any second reach field, nation-level military (BL-094's residual).

## S1 landed 2026-08-08

`building_type::military_base = 6` exists end-to-end: economics array bumped 6->7 with the Lua name-map row and an economy.lua entry (produces nothing, staffs at zero, dearer than a hub, cheaper than a launchpad); explicit `can_place` case (any non-ocean land, no deposit; the reach rule applies at the world level and the base earns NO anchor exemption); shield glyph in `icons::building` (filled, flat top tapering to a bottom point — echoes the unit chevron's martial reading without being confusable with the stroke-only unit marker) + ICONS.md catalogue row; named in presentation.cpp; offered in the tile build ledger and the primed-check list; `gameplay.build`'s dictionary entry updated (typed-args domain + reason_to_select) and the mirror regenerated; the verify seam's `place_mode` extended to arm launchpad / logistics_hub / military_base. Verified: buildings_rework_harness R6/R7 (19/19 PASS — placement rules, zero staffing, and ruling 3: a completed base is not a supply anchor and building one changes nothing in the reach field), plus a campaign `--verify` placement through the real construct path. **S2 (hire moves onto the base) and S3 (out-of-supply decay) remain open** — the item stays `designed`.

items.title: Construction ledger: expandable building groups, two-tier alphabetical sort
items.summary: Ben, 2026-08-08 live critique: with 15 extraction targets the flat candidate list no longer scans. Group candidates into expandable groups (Extraction / Processing / Infrastructure), sorted on a two-tier alphabetical system (group name, then row name) - explicitly NOT most-profit-first.

A dedicated scaffold/crane glyph drawn in place of the building silhouette while ticks_remaining > 0, instead of desaturating the final silhouette.

items.summary: Ben, 2026-08-08, live: selecting a building skips the Selection element, going straight to manage. SELECTION.md's click model says single-click SELECTS (fills the Selection element); double-click navigates/opens. A building click that jumps to management violates the model.

items.title: Player corp starts with a military base and one unit
items.summary: Ben, 2026-08-08: 'Let's start the player with a military unit and base.' Generation seeds the player corp with one military_base (BL-325 S1's building) on a home-province tile and one hired unit, so the military surface is discoverable from turn one rather than gated behind a first build.

items.title: Military points (base-produced) + a dedicated research building - the how-does-tech-get-done question
items.summary: Ben, 2026-08-08: 'We could use a military point system, produced by bases, for things like tech and hiring units. But we also don't have any measure for how tech gets done, so we need a dedicated building for that.' Two coupled design questions: (a) a military-point currency produced by bases, spendable on hiring and military tech; (b) the general tech-progress mechanism has NO production measure at all today - likely a dedicated research building. Design-owed: the answer must fit BL-087's constellation tech web (deeds open keystones) and BL-156's early tech pass, not invent a rival progression currency blind.
items.design:
Ben's prompt, 2026-08-08, recorded verbatim in summary. Open questions the design pass must settle: (1) is the military point a RESOURCE (stockpiled, market-invisible) or a RATE (like workforce)? (2) does the research building produce a general science measure, military points, or both keyed by building/recipe? (3) how does either interact with BL-087's deed-gated keystones - deeds are one-time acts, points are accumulation; do points buy band progress while deeds open keystones? (4) rival corps / the nation layer: who else accumulates? Sequencing: fits the v0.1.4 Techs stub minor (BL-156) as its concrete mechanism question.

## 2026-08-10 — re-versioned by the Sprints 8-12 plan (v0.1.11 -> v0.1.5)

Moved v0.1.11 -> v0.1.5. Military points + a dedicated research building answers "how does the militia get better", which belongs with the military minor rather than the laws one. Cut by Sprint 9 alongside BL-325 and BL-331.

## 2026-08-10 — design pass (Sprint 9), then re-versioned to v0.1.14

Answers Ben's four open questions from the 2026-08-08 filing. Kept out of Sprint 9's actual BUILD
scope deliberately (see the re-versioning note below) — this is the design half only, matching
the Delivery lifecycle's own split between settling a design and promoting it.

**1. Resource or rate?** RESOURCE — stockpiled, market-invisible, exactly like BL-107's eventual
save-format concerns treat a derived stock. A rate (workforce-style) implies continuous production
tied to staffing; military points are closer to RESEARCH POINTS in the genre this design pattern
comes from — banked, spent in lumps against a specific unlock, never decaying. A market-visible
resource would also be wrong on its own terms: military points are not something a rival corp buys
or sells, they are an internal capability accumulator. Read against BL-350 (the procurement seam,
filed the same sprint): the militia's *treasury* pays a company for equipment; military points are
a SEPARATE currency for the things a company cannot sell it — doctrine, training, unit-tech —
which is why the two do not collapse into one number even though both originate from Cr spend
somewhere upstream.

**2. What does the research building produce — general science, military points, or both?**
BOTH, keyed by building. Two distinct buildings, not one dual-output building: bases produce
military points (matching Ben's own framing — "produced by bases"), a dedicated RESEARCH building
(the "how does tech get done" half of the prompt) produces a general SCIENCE measure. Splitting
them is what lets BL-087's constellation (civilian bands/domains) and BL-315's conflict spine (the
militia's own capability ladder) draw from different taps rather than competing for the same one —
exactly the same reasoning BL-094's rewrite used to keep the militia's treasury separate from a
company's price. A corp with no research building still accumulates military points from its bases
alone; going further up BL-087's tree needs the research building built too.

**3. Points vs. deeds (BL-087's keystones)?** POINTS BUY BAND PROGRESS; DEEDS OPEN KEYSTONES —
Ben's own framing in the 2026-08-08 prompt already implies this split ("military point system...
for things like tech and hiring units" alongside "no measure for how tech gets done" as a SEPARATE
gap), and it matches BL-087's own settled shape (rings = bands opened by accumulation, keystones =
one-time deeds). Science/military points are the accumulator that advances a band; a deed is a
one-time act (first battle won, first base built past some threshold) that unlocks a keystone
WITHIN a reached band. Neither replaces the other — a corp that never fights can still accumulate
research points and progress bands, but keystones stay locked without the deed regardless of how
many points sit banked.

**4. Who else accumulates — rivals, the nation layer?** RIVAL CORPS, SYMMETRICALLY — the same
extension corp_ai's hiring got (BL-324's widening, io-standing-rules.md): military points are
produced by ANY corp's bases, not the player's alone, so a rival corp with a base is on the same
accumulation clock. THE NATION LAYER DOES NOT ACCUMULATE ITS OWN POOL under this design — the
"militia belongs to one nation" call (BL-094 § 2026-08-10) makes the militia (corp-tier entity)
the accumulator; a nation-level pool would imply nations doing research, which BL-094's rewrite
specifically retracted ("a militia does not run laboratories" — CONCEPT.md's 2026-08-10 note). If
a later item wants nation-level science (e.g., background nations advancing independently of any
militia), that is new scope, not implied by this one.

### Re-versioned v0.1.5 -> v0.1.14 (Sprint 9, same session)

Filed for v0.1.5 by the Sprints 8-12 plan on the reasoning that "how does the militia get better"
is a military-minor question. On working the actual design, both new buildings (the military-point
base output, the dedicated research building) are RESOURCE-TIER work — a new stockpiled quantity
with its own accumulation/spend rules, structurally the same kind of change BL-340 (processing
roster) already owns and was pulled forward into v0.1.14 for. Building this in v0.1.5 would
duplicate that machinery ahead of it existing; building it in v0.1.14 alongside BL-340 and BL-350
means one pass adds all the new stockpiled-quantity plumbing at once. The MILITARY-BASE half of
v0.1.5 (BL-325, BL-331) needed no such machinery and is unaffected by this move.
items.resolution: 2026-08-11 — complete (production side). New research_institute building_type + corporation_component.military_points/.science accumulators. Both military_base and research_institute credit their owning corp passively per tick once completed, symmetric across every corp. No spend mechanism (BL-087 constellation is the future sink) and no corp_ai build candidate for research_institute — both explicitly out of scope. New military_capability_harness (6/6 PASS); seven pre-existing harnesses plus the real build confirmed no regression. requirements.json § military-capability-points (R0-R3, all complete).

items.title: Nuclear weapons develop in-game - WW3 as a nuclear threat
items.summary: Ben, 2026-08-08: 'We should also ensure that nuclear weapons get developed in game, this is because WW3 is a nuclear threat.' The campaign's 1960 world must carry a live nuclear arc: weapons exist or are being developed, and the WW3-scale conflict the era implies is a nuclear threat, not a conventional one. Design-owed: touches the history ladder (HISTORY.md stage 6, the averted rupture - BL-223), the tech web (BL-087 keystones), and the conflict spine (BL-315).
items.design: Ben's prompt recorded 2026-08-08. The averted-rupture stage (BL-223) already frames a near-WW3; this item makes the NUCLEAR character of that threat explicit and playable: nations (not corps) develop nuclear weapons on the tech arc, their existence deters/looms over the Conflict pillar, and the v0.3.0 identity pivot (now the national private militia, NR-120) is where the player gains standing to touch that layer — deterrence and program-level decisions plausibly sit with the militia's home nation rather than the militia itself, which is a question this item still owes. Questions for the design pass: who holds them at campaign start (great powers from the BL-299 seed?), what the in-game development mechanism is (BL-087 keystone? nation-level program?), and what they DO mechanically (deterrence modifier on the conflict spine vs usable weapon - CONCEPT.md's tone leans deterrence).

items.title: Stage C: the conditioned dialogue layer over the corp_decision intent stream
items.summary: Ben's ruling 2026-08-08 (NR-094, AI_OPPONENT.md § 10g): the C-route feasibility note's Cicero-configuration recommendation is adopted as Stage C's concrete shape. Stage A/B (corp_ai.cpp's scored-utility core) stays the action generator indefinitely; Stage C is a small model (Cicero's reference point: 2.7B) conditioned on the corp_decision ring's winning-command + reason-code as an INTENT, generating in-character chat for the Public/private channels (§ 7) -- never emitting corp_command itself. This is the item that was flagged design-owed and unfiled as far back as the 2026-08-02 sprint note; filing it now that the ruling settles which Stage the model occupies.
items.design:
## What this item is

AI_OPPONENT.md § 7 named Stage C ('the LLM planner speaks in-character in channels') since 2026-07-26 but it was never decomposed into a buildable item -- it rode along as a stub inside BL-199's decomposition and then as an unfiled sprint-note flag. NR-094's ruling (§ 10g) gives it a concrete shape for the first time: Cicero's architecture, not a from-scratch design.

## Shape, per the ruling

- **Input**: the existing `corp_decision` ring (`{command, winning_score, runner_up, reason}`) -- already the intent stream a conditioned dialogue model consumes in Cicero's own architecture. No new export needed; BL-206's blackboard covers state, `corp_command_result` covers legality.
- **Output**: free-text chat into the Public channel or a private group (§ 7's existing chat surface, Stage-A templated today). The model NEVER calls `issue_command` -- it narrates decisions the scorer already made.
- **Model size**: Cicero's reference point is 2.7B (R2C2, encoder-decoder) -- comfortably inside both C1 (compressibility) and C2 (tractability) per the feasibility note's own math, with more room to spare than an action-emitting model would have (no constraint-tax exposure, since chat output isn't schema-constrained).
- **Corpus**: BL-279's trace collection, rescoped -- bootstrap from corp_ai.cpp's own decision ring (free, no cloud spend) rather than from cloud-played corp_command traces. Cloud inference's role, if any, is generating IN-CHARACTER TEXT for a given intent (a much cheaper, much lower-risk task than choosing the intent).
- **Persona bias**: `industrial_focus` (already generated per corp) supplies persona bias without authoring, per the feasibility note § 7 and AI_OPPONENT.md § 10c.3's observation that personality is emergent and should not be flattened.

## Open design questions (not settled by the ruling)

1. Sequencing against the v0.2.0 corp-AI arc -- does Stage C ship before or after BL-202/203's line closes out, or alongside it?
2. Whether BL-207's persona counsel packs (LLM-free, compiled offline) are a PRECURSOR to Stage C (ship personas without a runtime model first) or a permanently separate, cheaper tier that coexists with it.
3. Model attach mechanics: does Stage C run through the same MCP server (BL-278) as a client, or does it need its own local inference process wired directly into the chat surface? The feasibility note assumes MCP-attached; not yet verified against the chat surface's actual code path.

**Split out as their own items (2026-08-08), not carried here as footnotes:** BL-335 (measure the real per-decision token cost) and BL-336 (the goal-layer question, explicitly PARKED pending observed evidence). Neither blocks this item's promotion.

## Why design-owed, not designed

The SHAPE is settled (this write-up); the concrete build -- which channel triggers a Stage C utterance, how often, what the prompt template looks like, how it composes with Stage A's templated messages already in the same channel -- needs its own design pass before promotion.

items.title: The processing half of the buildings roster: new resource types with market, price and serialisation wiring
items.summary: Split out of BL-323 (buildings rework) at its v0.1.2 cut, 2026-08-09. BL-323's own completion note scopes this out in as many words: 'the processing-chain half of S1 (Chemical Plant, Electronics Lab, Fabricator, Assembly Plant, most Refinery outputs) needs NEW resource_type values with market/price/serialisation wiring -- a bigger item than Lua authoring, not attempted here.' Filed so closing BL-323 does not silently drop it.
items.design:
## Why this is not more Lua authoring

BL-323's S1 widened `k_extractable` from 4 to 15 targets with zero other code changes, because every consumer (placement, the build-mode target picker, the resource presentation table) was already generic over the list. The extraction half was therefore cheap. The processing half is not, and the reason is precise: the missing outputs are resources that **do not exist in the enum**.

Adding a `resource_type` value is not a Lua edit. It touches:

- **`components.hpp`** -- the enum itself, and any fixed-size per-resource array keyed off its cardinality.
- **`serialisation.cpp`** -- the save format. Resource ids are persisted; widening the enum is a save-format change, so BL-107 (save-format version) is adjacent and may want to land first or alongside.
- **market seeding and price bands** -- a new good with no seeded supply, demand or price band is a good that clears at a degenerate price. RESOURCES.md's tier model (raw -> refined -> product) says where each sits, but the seeding has to actually place it.
- **presentation** -- pip glyph and colour per ICONS.md, or the good renders as a hole in every readout.

## Scope

PRODUCTION.md designs 8 processing buildings; the registry loads 5 recipes after BL-323 added the Smelter's iron_nickel_ore -> steel. The gap is Chemical Plant, Electronics Lab, Fabricator, Assembly Plant and most Refinery outputs.

**Open question this item must settle first:** how many of RESOURCES.md's 31 resources actually need to exist for the prototype's chains to close, versus how many are Era 1 content that can stay unimplemented. The seven-resource prototype subset is the existing precedent for not building all 31 at once; the answer is probably a second small tranche, not the full set.

## Sequencing

After BL-323 (done). Wants a decision on BL-107 (save-format version) first, since this is the first deliberate save-format widening since that item was filed -- doing it blind is how a save-compat bug gets introduced with no version to gate on.

## 2026-08-10 - re-versioned by the Sprints 8-12 plan (v0.1.13 -> v0.1.14)

Moved v0.1.13 -> v0.1.14 (the new Procurement minor), per NR-120 ruling 3. The refocus says trade is coloured by military use and space equipment "initially" - so the processing roster stops being economic depth and becomes the goods the premise is made of. Without these resource types on the market, the colour is an assertion rather than a mechanic. Cut by Sprint 10 alongside the procurement/contract seam. Note this leaves v0.1.13 without its keystone; the five items remaining there stand on their own.

## 2026-08-10 - DESIGN PASS (settled; designed jointly with BL-350)

Designed together with BL-350 because they are mechanism and content for the same premise, and
each is incoherent alone. BL-094's rewrite says the militia "uses private companies to build
equipment for space": BL-350 is the buying, this item is the thing bought. Ship BL-350 alone and
the militia contracts for goods that do not exist; ship this alone and seven resources arrive with
no buyer that needs them - which is how BL-286's eight logistics goods landed inert and still are.

**The joint design's load-bearing decision:** `spacecraft_components` carries no background demand.
The militia's contracts are its only demand. That is what makes the coupling real rather than
thematic - the background economy does not want space equipment; a militia does.

### The admission rule (the durable half of the answer)

> A `resource_type` value must be consumed by an authored recipe, or be a terminal object some
> named actor contracts for or consumes. **No orphans.**

BL-286 is the cautionary precedent, named plainly: eight goods added with enum, serialisation and
base-price wiring, and no consumer. Two minors later grain, fodder, salt, transport_capacity,
charcoal, iron_blooms and bullion still have no mechanic that reads them. They cost save-format
width and readout space and return nothing.

Applying the rule: **IN** - silicon, refined_copper, ree_alloy (consumed by the Tier-3 recipes,
each also rescuing a dead raw); alloys, electronics (consumed by the Assembly Plant);
spacecraft_components (terminal - the militia's contract object); machinery (terminal, and the
Fabricator's *alternative* to alloys - it makes that building a choice rather than a forced path).
**OUT** - liquid oxygen (already folded into both Chemical Plant recipes by BL-308; nothing outside
the plant would hold it); clean water, building materials, consumer goods, medical supplies,
utilities (habitability goods whose consumer is deferred from the prototype).

### The real content is pricing, not the enum

The filed design above leads with the enum extension as the expensive part. **That is backwards.**
Every per-resource array is already sized off `resource_count` (components.hpp, world_gen_config.hpp,
recipe_registry.hpp, law.hpp, planetology.hpp) - there is no fixed-width `std::array<float, 32>`
anywhere in src/world/, which is why BL-286's eight-good extension needed no per-array edit.

The expensive half is that **three of the four raws the new recipes consume cannot be bought.**
silica, copper_ore and rare_earth_ore carry base_price 0, and clear_markets skips every resource
with no base price. A processing building auto-buys its input shortfall from the market, so a
Refinery pointed at silica draws against a market that will never supply it and the recipe is dead
on arrival. **This item's actual centre of gravity is closing the minable-but-unsellable
asymmetry;** the enum extension is a precondition, not the work.

### The authored tranche

Seven new enum values (32 -> 39), appended in tier order:

| Value | Tier | Recipe | Building |
|---|---|---|---|
| silicon | 2 | silica 2.0 -> 1.0 | Refinery |
| refined_copper | 2 | copper_ore 2.0 -> 1.0 | Smelter |
| ree_alloy | 2 | rare_earth_ore 2.0 -> 1.0 | Refinery |
| machinery | 3 | steel 1.0 + refined_copper 1.0 -> 1.0 | Fabricator |
| alloys | 3 | steel 1.0 + ree_alloy 1.0 -> 1.0 | Fabricator |
| electronics | 3 | silicon 1.0 + refined_copper 1.0 + ree_alloy 0.5 -> 1.0 | Electronics Lab |
| spacecraft_components | 3 | alloys 2.0 + electronics 1.0 -> 1.0 | Assembly Plant |

Six base prices on existing raws, closing the asymmetry: coal 2.0 (also the steel reagent - see the
correction below), silica 2.0, copper_ore 3.0, rare_earth_ore 6.0 ("low concentration, high base
price"), iron_nickel_ore 3.0 (recipe 6 already consumes it and it had no market),
platinum_group_metals 40.0 (terminal by design - RESOURCES.md calls it the belt's primary
high-value trade good; its job is to be sold).

Seven base prices for the new goods, on a deliberate ladder - silicon 5.0 (1.25x margin over input
cost), refined_copper 7.5 (1.25x), ree_alloy 16.0 (1.33x), machinery 22.0 (1.42x), alloys 34.0
(1.42x), electronics 29.0 (1.41x), spacecraft_components 140.0 (1.44x). The margin widens up the
tiers, which is the intended shape: Tier 3 is where RESOURCES.md promises "widest price divergence",
and spacecraft_components at 140.0 sits **56x iron ore**. That ladder is the value gradient the
whole space-equipment premise rests on.

These are first-cut authored constants in the existing style, not balanced figures. The shipped
table is not internally consistent either - food_rations at 6.0 from 2x3.0 of agricultural produce
is exactly break-even - so the tranche should not be held to a standard the existing seven do not
meet. Retune by playtest.

### Background demand - DELETED from this item (2026-08-10, sequencing change)

The design pass originally specified substrate `demand_basket` weights plus an abstract
refined-goods capacity in `inject_substrate_demand`, and named it the risk step. **That step is not
built here.** Ben's 2026-08-10 call put the living world (BL-365) first, and BL-365 removes
`inject_substrate_demand` outright - so building this would be building it twice.

Background production and consumption for the seven new goods is **BL-365's** responsibility. The
hazard transfers rather than disappearing: a good with demand and no supply pegs at 4x base
forever, and under real background industry that means no firm produces it. BL-365 carries it as an
explicit failure condition. The intended demand *shape* (machinery heaviest, then electronics,
refined_copper, silicon, alloys; spacecraft_components deliberately zero) is retained here as input
to BL-365's calibration.

### Scope explicitly excluded

Named `building_type` enum values (Refinery, Fabricator, Electronics Lab, Assembly Plant) - they
stay recipes on the generic processing_facility exactly as the shipped five do. Habitability goods
and their buildings. Retuning the shipped seven base prices. Deposit generation changes - every raw
this item prices already has authored deposits (BL-040).

### Corrections this pass owes elsewhere

- **This item's own `files` list named `src/world/serialisation.cpp`, which does not exist** -
  `find src -iname "*serial*"` returns nothing. Corrected on the item.
- **BL-107's "no flat-binary serialiser exists" is stale**, and the dependency it implies is live
  again rather than vacuous. As of BL-293 there are two such streams - history_log.{hpp,cpp} and
  order_book.{hpp,cpp} - both already carrying the magic + version header BL-107 specifies.
  `read_order_book` rejects a resource byte outside the known `resource_type` range, so widening
  the enum moves a validation boundary in shipped serialised state. Not a blocker, but the version
  bump is a real step.
- **PRODUCTION.md and recipes.lua disagree on the steel recipe.** The doc's Smelter table says iron
  ore + coal (reagent) -> steel; recipes.lua id 1 is `{ iron_ore = 2.0 }` with no coal. Pricing coal
  makes this worth reconciling in the same pass - recommend adding the reagent, since it gives coal
  a consumer that the admission rule would otherwise require.

### Requirement sketch (owed at promotion)

`headless`, extending econ_harness or a new resource_chain_harness: a rollout in which every one of
the seven new goods is produced, priced and cleared at least once, **and no priced good sits pegged
at the 4x band ceiling for the whole run**.
items.resolution: 2026-08-11 — complete. Seven new resource_type values (silicon, refined_copper, ree_alloy, machinery, alloys, electronics, spacecraft_components) land: enum, base prices, recipes, UI presentation, docs. Six pre-existing raws gain base prices, closing the minable-but-unsellable asymmetry. Steel gains a coal reagent (closes NR-158). New resource_chain_harness verifies the chain; determinism/order-book/world-audit/construction/econ harnesses and the real build all confirmed green, ai_skill_harness bit-identical to baseline. requirements.json § processing-chain-roster (R0-R4, all complete). Background demand for the roster is BL-365's responsibility, not built here.

items.title: Run the from-cold configure check on the Windows box, where the SDL3 TLS revocation failure actually happens
blocked_on: access to the Windows development machine
items.summary: Split out of BL-302 at the v0.1.8 cut. BL-302 settled and implemented the dependency-acquisition posture (seeded FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_<dep> cache + a documented from-cold check), but the fault that opened it -- a schannel TLS revocation failure downloading SDL3 -- is Windows-specific and does NOT reproduce on Linux, where a from-cold configure succeeds in ~74s. So the fix is untested against the actual symptom. PARKED 2026-08-09 (Ben): blocked on being at the Windows machine, so it was travelling with every cut and appearing in each done-definition as open work. parked:true / priority F is the project existing flag for not-scheduled; unpark the moment that box is to hand.
items.design:
One command, on the Windows machine, from `DEVELOPMENT_PRACTICES.md` § Dependency acquisition:

```
IO_DEPS_CACHE=/nonexistent cmake -S . -B <tmp>/build -DFETCHCONTENT_BASE_DIR=<tmp>/deps -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
```

`IO_DEPS_CACHE=/nonexistent` is load-bearing: without it the seeded cache satisfies the configure and the check proves nothing.

**Two outcomes, and they lead different ways.**

- **It fails with the schannel revocation error** -- the posture is vindicated: seed `_deps_cache` from a working tree once, and that machine never needs the network at configure time again. Confirm the seeded path then works there.
- **It succeeds** -- the original failure was transient or environmental (AV TLS interception, a cert-chain change since), and BL-302's machinery is insurance rather than a fix. Record that, because it changes how much the cache is worth carrying.

Either way the answer is cheap and the item is a verification, not a build. Blocked only on being at that machine.

items.title: Politics MVP: the nation-pair relationship axis, generated from existing character, with one consumer that actually reads it
items.summary: Prototype-enabler filed 2026-08-09 to make v0.1.6 cuttable. BL-158's own 2026-08-02 note records that most of the politics stub was already dissolved into other items, leaving ONE axis genuinely unowned: inter-nation relationships. This builds that axis and -- the part that matters -- gives it a consumer, because a data stub nothing reads is indistinguishable from no stub at all.
items.design:
## What is actually left of v0.1.6

BL-158 was a data-model stub for political character, relationships and lever slots. Its 2026-08-02
settlement records that most of it dissolved: political character already exists in nation
generation, and the lever slots went to BL-155 (laws) and BL-094 (the governing actor). The
residual is the **relationship axis** -- how two nations stand toward each other -- and nothing
owns it.

## The rule this item is built on

**A stub nothing reads is indistinguishable from no stub.** The failure mode for a
"data-model stub" minor is shipping serialisable records that no code path consults, declaring the
model positioned, and discovering at v0.3.0 that the shape was wrong because nothing ever exercised
it. So this item deliberately includes a consumer, and the consumer is the acceptance criterion.

## Scope

**In:** a symmetric per-nation-pair relationship scalar; derivation at world generation from
political character and shared borders that already exist; ONE consumer that changes observable
behaviour; a headless harness. **Out:** diplomacy verbs (BL-297), treaties, war declaration, any
runtime nation actor (BL-094 re-specifies that from the new player identity), AI decision-making.

## Shape

One scalar per unordered pair, seeded deterministically. Derive it from what generation already
produces rather than rolling it fresh -- the ladder's fragmentation outcome, shared border length,
and the political character already assigned. Two nations that share a long contested border and
opposed characters start cold; two that share neither start neutral. **Derived, not narrated**, which
is the same discipline HISTORY.md's ladder is held to.

Storage is a flat symmetric structure keyed by the pair, not a per-nation list of opinions --
asymmetric relationships are a real design option but they double the state and nothing in the
prototype needs them yet. Say so explicitly so v0.3.0 knows it was a choice.

## The consumer -- pick the cheapest honest one

**Convoy/trade access across a hostile border.** The logistics layer already computes
terrain-weighted routes with road discounts and already knows which nation owns a tile, so a
relationship term is a modifier on an existing cost function rather than a new system -- the same
shape BL-323's reach rule took, and the reason that one was affordable.

The player-visible consequence: trading across a cold border costs more, so the political map
starts mattering to the economic one. That is also the first time politics reaches something the
player already cares about, which is what makes v0.1.6 worth cutting rather than filing.

## The design test

BL-094 asks whether the system reaches military as well as economic outcomes. Relationships are
the axis a conflict layer reads FIRST -- who may cross whom, who supplies whom (BL-315's supply
lines as live targets). So the axis must be shaped as a general standing between nations, not as a
trade modifier that happens to be called a relationship. The MVP's single consumer is economic
because that is what exists to consume it; the TYPE must not encode that.

## Verification

`tools/verify/relationship_harness.cpp`: every nation pair has exactly one entry and it is
symmetric; the same seed produces the same matrix; a cold pair raises cross-border convoy cost by
the stated term while a neutral pair does not; no self-pair exists; the derivation reacts to
shared-border length in the stated direction.

items.title: The procurement/contract seam — the militia buys equipment from a private company that can quote, delay, or refuse
items.summary: Filed at BL-094's 2026-08-10 rewrite (NR-120). The mechanic the militia refocus actually invents: contracting a private company for equipment rather than building it internally. A counterparty with a price, a lead time, and a possible refusal — not a purchase order against an unlimited market and not a second wallet. The closest existing shape is BL-280 (negotiated tax rate), which bargains a rate with a different counterparty (the home nation, not a supplier); the two should be designed alongside each other since both are 'the player negotiates with an entity that can say no' dressed differently. Sits in the new v0.1.14 Procurement minor alongside BL-340 (the resource-tier roster that supplies what gets contracted for).
items.design:
**Status:** designed 2026-08-10, jointly with BL-340. Filed at BL-094's rewrite (NR-120).

### What this item owns

The mechanic BL-094's 2026-08-10 rewrite introduces and nothing existing covers: the militia
contracts a private company to build it equipment, rather than the equipment simply existing on a
market it can always afford, or being produced by an economic arm it owns outright (the 2026-07-04
chartered-corp/shared-treasury design, retracted by the rewrite).

### The spine

> **A procurement contract is a build order placed with someone else.**

BL-095 already ships the whole pacing model: commit on affordability, draw materials per tick as
real market demand, progress at the rate the market can supply, stretch up to ~10x or pause, pay
across the build rather than up front. A contract is that same object with two changes - the
materials are drawn against the **supplier's** market, and the output is delivered to the
**buyer's** pool.

This is the design's main claim to legibility. It reuses a shipped, understood, already-tuned
mechanism instead of inventing a second payment-and-pacing shape, and it means a stalled contract
stalls for a reason the player already understands from construction.

### The four filed questions, answered

**Q1 - Does the treasury debit on order, on delivery, or split?**
**Split: a deposit on order, the remainder drawn per tick across the lead time** - mirroring BL-095
exactly. Deposit fraction is a Lua constant (`economy.procurement.deposit_fraction`, first cut
0.25). Both alternatives fail concretely: on-delivery-only makes ordering free, so the dominant
strategy is to order from every supplier and cancel all but the fastest; on-order-only makes the
contract a spot purchase with a delay, where the counterparty's price and refusal do no work and it
collapses back into the order book.

**Q2 - Is refusal a hard block or a payable penalty?**
**A hard decline at quote time, with a stated reason. Not payable-through.** Refusal is not a wall:
it is priced information. A declining supplier states why, and other suppliers may still quote, so
the player routes around a refusal rather than buying through it. A payable override would collapse
refusal into a surcharge, making the counterparty a vending machine with a markup - precisely what
BL-094's rewrite retracted the shared treasury to avoid. **If everything is buyable, there is no
counterparty.**

Four decline conditions: **no capacity** (supplier holds no completed building that can produce the
good); **no input access** (supplier's market cannot supply the recipe inputs - reuses BL-095's
paused test); **law/embargo** (a `condition_set` (BL-342, shipped v0.1.3) evaluates false); and
**reputation floor** (pair standing below a threshold). The third is the useful one: condition_set
is shipped generic predicate machinery, so the law layer reaches procurement for free. That is
BL-315's "what the militia must answer to" axis arriving without new machinery, and it is the
strongest single argument that this seam sits in the right place.

**Q3 - Does reputation persist?**
**Yes, minimally: one scalar per (buyer, supplier) pair, moved by completed and cancelled contracts
only.** Effects are deliberately narrow - it shifts the quoted price within a band and breaks ties
in quote ordering. It does not unlock exclusive goods and does not by itself gate access beyond the
Q2 floor. The reasoning both ways: a persistent scalar is what makes a *sequence* of contracts a
strategy rather than each one an isolated purchase; but the moment it gates access to goods it is a
tech tree wearing a relationship's clothes, and BL-087 already owns that job. **Read alongside
BL-345** (politics MVP relationship axis, v0.1.6) - if BL-345 lands first, this reads its axis
instead of storing a second one.

**Q4 - Parallel to, or an extension of, BL-037's preferred-seller routing?**
**A parallel object on the same seam - not an order-book entry.** Written against BL-293 (landed),
which made the order book world state, had clear_markets read it directly, and joined three verbs
to corp_command (enum 11 wide, append-only). A contract cannot be a book entry: the book is
price-time priority over anonymous asks, with no representation for a named counterparty or a lead
time. But procurement joins the **same command seam**, for the reason BL-293 gives - so the
player's press and the AI's command are one implementation rather than two that agree.

Three new verbs, appended (enum 11 -> 14, append-only per BL-293's convention): `request_quote`
(ask a named supplier for price + lead time on a quantity), `accept_quote` (convert a live quote
into a contract; debits the deposit), `cancel_contract` (terminate in flight; forfeits the deposit,
moves reputation). Plus a **fourth flat-binary stream** after history_log and order_book, following
both exactly - magic IOPC, a version, count-prefixed records, rejection rather than
reinterpretation.

The composition, stated once: the contract's per-tick material draw enters market demand exactly as
BL-095's construction draw does, so the supplier's own inputs clear through the existing order book
at market prices. **Procurement is a layer over the market, not a second market.**

### Lead time is derived, not authored

`lead_time_ticks = base_ticks x ceil(quantity / supplier_throughput_per_tick)`, where throughput is
what the supplier's relevant buildings actually produce. A bigger order takes longer; a supplier
with real capacity is faster.

This gives the mechanic a second job worth having: **the quote is an intelligence channel.** You
learn something about a rival's industrial capacity by asking it for a price. That is legitimate
under BL-068 (competitor internals private, markets public), because the supplier volunteers the
figure in its own quote rather than the player reading its internals. It is a new, diegetic route
through the activity fog, and DISCOVERY.md should pick it up when this lands.

### The buyer is not the militia yet - and does not need to be

This item was filed `blocked_on: [BL-094]`. **That block is dropped**, and the reason is a version
inversion worth stating: this item targets v0.1.14, BL-094 targets v0.3.0. An item cannot be
blocked on one that lands three minors later without being silently unbuildable.

The block dissolves on inspection, because **the seam is buyer-agnostic.** A contract is between two
corp-like entities holding a treasury and a pool. Today both are `corporation`. When BL-094's
militia entity lands it becomes the natural buyer with no change to the seam. `requires: [BL-094]`
stays as a read-alongside; what BL-094 supplies is the *narrative* - why the buyer does not simply
build the thing itself - and narrative does not block a mechanism.

### Relationship to BL-280 (negotiated tax rate)

The shared shape is real: quote -> accept/decline -> standing term, pointed at different
counterparties. But BL-280's actual blocker is untouched by this design - its open question is what
the nation wants in return for a lower rate, the counterparty cost without which the tax dial is
free money. This item answers the analogous question structurally (the supplier wants price, lead
time and standing), which does not transfer to a sovereign granting a tax concession.
**Recommendation: this item does not wait for BL-280.** Extract a shared negotiation primitive when
the second user actually exists - not speculatively, on one user, against an item that is still
design-owed and difficulty 5.

### Scope explicitly excluded

The militia entity itself (BL-094, v0.3.0). Unit materiel consumption - what a fielded unit draws
per tick; BL-332's military points are a separate currency and stay separate. A negotiation dialogue
(BL-334, Stage C) - the quote is a number with a reason string, not a conversation. Tax bargaining
(BL-280). Multi-round haggling - a quote is take-it-or-leave-it in this cut; counter-offers are a
later item if the seam proves worth deepening.

### 2026-08-10 - sequencing: this lands AFTER the living world

Ben's call the same day put BL-365 (background industry) first, cutting v0.1.13 in Sprint 10; this
pair moves to Sprint 11 / v0.1.14. The reason is specific to this item: the counterparty model above
- a supplier that can refuse, with the player routing around the refusal to another quote - needs
suppliers to choose between. Against the pre-BL-365 world (8 lean corps, ~24 buildings on 15,120
tiles) "another supplier may still quote" is frequently false, and the mechanic would ship correct
but unexercised. That is the shape of Sprint 9's `hire_unit`, which shipped correct and was never
once observed firing across five harness seeds (NR-121).

### Requirement sketch (owed at promotion)

`headless`, a new procurement_harness: one contract quoted, accepted, paced and delivered end to end
with the treasury debited in the split shape; plus one decline observed for **each** of the four
refusal conditions. Sprint 9 shipped a done-definition that honestly recorded a path never observed
firing; this requirement is written so that does not recur.
items.resolution: 2026-08-11 — complete (mechanism only, matching the item's own excluded scope). Three new corp_verbs (request_quote/accept_quote/cancel_contract) on the shared command seam; split-payment contracts (deposit + paced remainder); four distinguishable decline reasons (capacity, input access, embargo via condition_set, reputation floor); a standing (buyer,supplier) reputation scalar; a fourth flat-binary stream (procurement.{hpp,cpp}, magic IOPC) modelled on order_book. One named simplification: fixed-schedule pacing rather than BL-095's market-gated rate. New procurement_harness (18/18 PASS); eight pre-existing harnesses plus the real build confirmed no regression. requirements.json § procurement-contract-seam (R0-R4, all complete).

items.title: Corporate borders read as hex-grid territory, not a circle around the seat
items.summary: Ben, 2026-08-08: 'Currently, we render a circle around the centre of the corp, but this basically tells us nothing. Instead, let's map the corporation borders directly onto the hex grid, and we can more easily see what is and isn't a valid move.' [Renumbered from BL-325 on 2026-08-10: that id was taken by the shipped military-base item (BL-325 MILITARY_BASE_AND_SUPPLY) while this branch sat unmerged. Delivery rule — keep the earlier/shared item, renumber the newcomer.]
items.design:
THE PRESENT BEHAVIOUR. `draw_corp_border` (src/ui/body_surface_canvas.cpp, BL-182 lineage) draws
the player's always-on border and, under the Corporation lens, each rival's, as a single
`dl->AddCircle` of radius `influence_range * hex_size * zoom` centred on the corp's persisted
`hq_building` tile, plus an HQ glyph. One circle, one radius, per corp per body.

WHY IT TELLS YOU NOTHING (Ben's word, and it is the right one). The circle is a picture of a
SCALAR. `influence_range` is fixed at generation and never grows, so the ring is the same shape
on an island as on a continent, and it is drawn in screen space over a hex grid, so the tiles it
appears to contain are not the tiles any rule would contain. The player reads it and learns one
number they were already told. Worse, it is about to become actively misleading: BL-323 makes
placement depend on LOGISTICS REACH, a per-tile weighted cost from the nearest supply anchor
(world::body_reach_cost), which is a field with a genuinely irregular shape - it follows roads,
stops at coastlines, and is infinite where nothing is reachable. A circle drawn beside that field
asserts a boundary the gate does not enforce, which is the exact failure the build surfaces were
just fixed for: a tile offered and then refused at commit reads as a broken build rather than a
rule.

THE CHANGE. Render the border as the SET OF TILES, tinted and outlined on the hex grid, rather
than as a radius. The per-tile answer already exists - this is a rendering change over an
existing field, not a new mechanic. Two questions are open and are the design owed:

Q1 - WHICH SET? Three candidates, and they are not the same set: (a) tiles within
`influence_range` hexes of the seat, i.e. the honest hex rendering of what is drawn today;
(b) tiles whose `body_reach_cost` is inside the corp's logistics budget, i.e. where the corp
could actually SUPPLY a building, which is what 'a valid move' means once BL-323 lands; (c) the
union of tiles the corp holds plus their neighbours. Ben's stated purpose - 'more easily see what
is and isn't a valid move' - argues for (b), which makes this item a consumer of BL-323's reach
field rather than a reskin of BL-182's radius. Confirm before building.

Q2 - WHOSE, AND UNDER WHAT LENS? Today the player's ring is always-on chrome and rivals appear
only under the Corporation lens. A filled tile region is far heavier than an outline, so
always-on tinting for the player may fight every other overlay. Likely answer: draw the OUTLINE
(border edges only - the edges of the region, not every hex edge inside it) always-on, and the
fill only under the Corporation lens. That also keeps the visual grammar consistent with the
Country lens's national borders.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE. Border-edge extraction over a hex raster is the standard trick: for each
tile in the set, draw only those of its six edges whose neighbour is NOT in the set. The body
tile raster index (world::body_tile_grid) already gives O(1) neighbour lookup, and the canvas
already handles horizontal wrap by drawing k copies at `period_px` - the edge pass must be inside
that same k loop or the border will not wrap with the map.

SEQUENCING. Depends on BL-323 if Q1 resolves to (b): the reach budget must be the authoritative
gate before a surface can honestly draw it. If Ben picks (a), it is independent and small.

---

## SETTLED 2026-08-12 (Ben, review-queue Q&A resolving NR-139)

Both open questions are answered, and the second went further than the recommendation.

**Q1 - which tile set is the border: (b) the logistics-reach budget.** The border is the set of tiles the corp can actually reach, so it draws what 'a valid move' costs rather than a circle around a scalar. This is the reading Ben's original objection pointed at - the influence-range rendering (a) would have been an honest hex version of a picture that already told him nothing.

Consequence for sequencing: this item now **depends on BL-323** (the buildings/logistics rework that owns the reach field) and cannot land before it. blocked_on set accordingly. It is no longer the small independent reskin option (a) would have made it.

**Q2 - how heavy: outline AND fill, only under the Corporation lens.** Not the recommended outline-always/fill-on-lens split. The border is not always-on canvas chrome at all: it appears when the player asks the Corporation lens the question it answers, and is absent otherwise. This is the stronger form of the same argument that opened the entry - a border occupying the canvas full-time had better be telling you something full-time, and this one is not.

That also removes the overlay-conflict worry the question raised: nothing to fight with other overlays if it only draws under its own lens.

Note for whoever builds it: BL-372 (lens-keyed selection) makes the Corporation lens also change what a click selects. The two share a surface and should be checked together - under that lens the border shows the reach and a click grabs the corp.
